column5: source
column6: target

column5: No, it's not that. There's just so much going on.\nAre you sure that won't interfere with anything...?
column6: 不，不是那样。只是事情太多了。\n你确定那不会影响到什么……？

column5: Of course not! I think we're smarter than that.\nBesides, it was perfect. We shared a Mazean Apple!
column6: 当然不会！我觉得我们没那么蠢。\n再说，那太完美了。我们分享了一个马泽奥苹果！

column5: Wow, how romantic.
column6: 哇，真浪漫。

column5: You had to be there!
column6: 你得在场才能体会！

column5: I think I'll pass...\nIt's good to see you enjoying yourself, though.\nThere's just too much on my mind for that kind of stuff.
column6: 我还是算了吧……\n不过看到你这么开心，挺好的。\n只是我脑子里装的事太多，没心思想那些。

column5: Just wait until we get to the Rebel HQ, Valessa.\nIt'll be a life of luxury, you'll see. There'll be plenty of time!
column6: 等我们到了反抗军总部再说吧，瓦莱莎。\n会是奢华的生活，你就看着吧。有的是时间！

column5: We can dream...
column6: 做梦还是可以的……

column5: This party banter is due to your relationship with Fortaime.
column6: 这段队伍闲聊源于你与福泰姆的关系。

column5: So this is the \"spirit idol\" of Mazeo.{w}\nAt least, that's what they thought until recently.{w}\nI can see why they'd make that mistake, actually.
column6: 这就是马泽奥的“灵像”了。{w}\n至少，直到最近他们一直是这么认为的。{w}\n其实我能理解他们为什么会认错。

column5: It sure looks like a spirit idol.{w}\nWell, a dying one, at least.
column6: 它看起来确实像一尊灵像。{w}\n嗯，至少是一尊濒死的。

column5: But to think, the real one is deep underground.{w}\nAnd allegedly, it's massive — and full of energy.{w}\nIt'd be the first time I saw an active spirit idol.
column6: 可想想吧，真正的那个深埋地下。{w}\n据说它巨大无比——还充满能量。{w}\n那会是我第一次见到活跃的灵像。

column5: Pews line the church, full of dust, and signs of neglect.{w}\nIt was almost a statement that no one cared about The Triumvirate.{w}\nThat was a bit hopeful to see. Now I know why Damek likes this place.
column6: 教堂里排满长椅，积满灰尘，处处透着荒废。{w}\n这几乎就是在宣告，没人在乎三人执政团。{w}\n看到这让人有点欣慰。现在我明白达梅克为什么喜欢这里了。

column5: It doesn't look like anybody has been here in ages.{w}\nHowever, a dust-free trail leads to the door at the back.{w}\nIt's clear that only The Rebels have been making use of it.
column6: 看起来好久没人来过了。{w}\n不过，一条没有灰尘的痕迹通向后门。{w}\n显然只有反抗军一直在使用这里。

column5: Continuing their adventure through the docks, Sovy keeps close to Shane.{w}\nLeading everybody into a secluded back alley, he lets out a loud sigh.{w}\nIt was nice to get away from all the noise. Mazeans were obnoxious.
column6: 他们的冒险在码头继续，索维紧跟在肖恩身边。{w}\n他把大家带进一条僻静的后巷，重重叹了口气。{w}\n能远离那些喧嚣真好。马泽奥人真讨厌。

column5: What gives...?\nThis isn't the way to Valinorth.\nBut I guess you {i}do{/i} like going backwards.
column6: 搞什么……？\n这可不是去瓦利诺斯的路。\n不过我猜你{i}确实{/i}喜欢走回头路。

column5: Oh, we'll get there yet.\nI just have some business to tend to.\nShane, can I talk to you alone for a moment?
column6: 哦，我们总会到的。\n我只是有点事要处理。\n肖恩，我能单独跟你聊一会儿吗？

column5: Shane nods, and follows Sovy deeper into the alleyway.{w}\nHalin takes the note and stands guard, ensuring their privacy.
column6: 肖恩点点头，跟着索维往巷子深处走去。{w}\n哈林会意，守在一旁放哨，确保他们不被打扰。

column5: Look, something important has come up.\nYou're aware of our moles within The Rebellion, right?
column6: 听着，出了件重要的事。\n你知道我们在反抗军里安插了内线吧？

column5: {i}Alleged{/i} moles.
column6: {i}所谓的{/i}内线。

column5: Yes.\nWell, I found this at our drop point.\nI think it's something you'll be interested in.
column6: 是的。\n嗯，我在我们的交接点发现了这个。\n我觉得你会感兴趣。

column5: Sovy holds out a letter, prompting Shane to take it.
column6: 索维递出一封信，示意肖恩接过去。

column5: It's a letter written by Damek?\nWhy is this important...?
column6: 这是达梅克写的信？\n这有什么重要的……？

column5: Just read it, Shane.\nIt's from Damek to Valinorth's Elder.\nIt seems your capture was just part of his plan.
column6: 读就是了，肖恩。\n是达梅克写给瓦利诺斯长老的。\n看来你被俘只是他计划的一部分。

column5: What!?
column6: 什么！？

column5: Shane keeps reading the letter, his eyes shooting wide open.{w}\nEvery word was like a knife to the heart. He was betrayed.
column6: 肖恩继续读着信，双眼骤然睁大。{w}\n每个字都像刀插进心脏。他被背叛了。

column5: He {i}wanted{/i} me to get captured...?\nLook at this — it says he hates me!?
column6: 他{i}想{/i}让我被俘……？\n你看这个——上面说他恨我！？

column5: I'm sorry you had to find out this way.\nBut your \"mission\" was only a cover.\nHe wanted to kill you off, Shane.
column6: 很抱歉让你以这种方式得知。\n但你的“任务”只是个幌子。\n他想除掉你，肖恩。

column5: That's not true. I refuse to believe this.\nI know Damek. He wouldn't do this to me!
column6: 不是真的。我不信。\n我了解达梅克。他不会这样对我！

column5: Are you sure about that...?\nIt makes sense when you think about it.\nHe sent you there to gain intel, right?
column6: 你确定……？\n仔细想想就说得通了。\n他派你去那里是为了搜集情报，对吧？

column5: Yeah...
column6: 是啊……

column5: He already had all the intel he needed.\nThat was the purpose of The Exodus Raid.\nThey mapped out our entire castle, Shane.
column6: 他早就拿到了所有需要的情报。\n那正是“流亡突袭”的目的。\n他们摸清了我们整座城堡的布局，肖恩。

column5: What intel is there left for you to gather...?\nNone. Damek just wanted you out of the way.
column6: 还有什么情报需要你去搜集……？\n没有。达梅克只是想把你支开。

column5: No...
We were merciful enough to give you a chance, Shane.\nWe could've killed you, but we still found value in your life.\nI think that's way more than anything Damek can say.
column6: 我们够仁慈，给了你一个机会，肖恩。\n我们本可以杀了你，但我们仍觉得你的命有价值。\n我想这比达梅克能说的任何话都强得多。

column5: It really does look like his handwriting...
column6: 那真的很像他的笔迹……

column5: I have no reason to lie to you, Shane.\nI know what it's like to have your world torn apart.\nIt seems like all hope is lost, doesn't it?
column6: 我没理由骗你，肖恩。\n我知道世界被撕裂是什么滋味。\n感觉所有希望都没了，对吧？

column5: What should I do...?
column6: 我该怎么办……？

column5: You {i}were{/i} planning to run away, weren't you?\nMaybe you thought you could lose us in the crowd?\nIt's a good idea — but there's no home left for you there.
column6: 你{i}本来{/i}打算逃跑，对吧？\n也许你以为能在人群里甩掉我们？\n主意不错——但那里已经没有你的家了。

column5: Why did you wait until {i}now{/i} to show me?
column6: 你为什么等到{i}现在{/i}才给我看？

column5: Because I have a favor to ask of you, Shane.\nAnd remember, I would {i}never{/i} abandon you.\nI've had every opportunity to kill you.
column6: 因为我有个忙要请你帮，肖恩。\n记住，我{i}绝不会{/i}抛弃你。\n我随时都有机会杀了你。

column5: A favor...?
column6: 帮忙……？

column5: Sovy takes back the letter while he watches Shane fight back tears.{w}\nIt was a hard thing to accept — being disowned by your family.{w}\nBut it was a pain that Sovy knew all too well. He could relate.
column6: 索维收回信，看着肖恩强忍泪水。{w}\n被自己的家人抛弃——这是很难接受的事。{w}\n但那种痛，索维再清楚不过。他感同身受。

column5: He didn't respond just yet. He watched a silent rage build up within Shane.{w}\nThat would be perfect. For rage was an invaluable tool on the battlefield.{w}\nWith a smirk, Sovy finally broke his silence, placing a hand on Shane.
column6: 他没有立刻回应。他看着无声的怒火在肖恩心中积聚。{w}\n那再好不过了。因为在战场上，愤怒是无价的工具。{w}\n索维微微一笑，终于打破沉默，把手搭在肖恩身上。

column5: Don't worry, I'll still let you visit Damek and The Rebels.\nIt's just — I have something {i}different{/i} in mind for you.\nA chance to \"pay him back\", if you'd be so inclined.
column6: 别担心，我还是会让你去见达梅克和反抗军的。\n只是——我为你准备了{i}不一样{/i}的东西。\n一个“回报他”的机会，如果你愿意的话。

column5: Shane's fists trembled in anger.{w}\nIn this moment, he was right where Sovy wanted him.
column6: 肖恩的拳头因愤怒而颤抖。{w}\n这一刻，他正处在索维想让他待的位置。

column5: Yeah. \nI'll do it...
column6: 好。\n我干……

column5: Gryz sits at his desk with his head in his hands, emotionally drained.{w}\nLillith enters his office, showing concern, but decides to talk business instead.
column6: 格瑞兹坐在桌前，双手抱头，心力交瘁。{w}\n莉莉丝走进他的办公室，神情担忧，但还是决定谈正事。

column5: Gryz, sir. \nThe papers have been sent back out.\nAlex and Nada should know momentarily.
column6: 格瑞兹，先生。\n文件已经重新发出去了。\n亚历克斯和娜达应该很快就会知道。

column5: Slightly shocked, Gryz shakes his head, and rests his hands on his desk.
column6: 格瑞兹微微一怔，摇了摇头，把双手放到桌上。

column5: Thank you, Lillith.\nI couldn't do this without you.
column6: 谢谢你，莉莉丝。\n没有你我做不成这些。

column5: You give me too much credit.\nI'm just a glorified paper pusher.\nYou do all the heavy lifting, you know.
column6: 你太抬举我了。\n我不过是个体面点的文书。\n重活都是你在干，你知道的。

column5: He sighs, and rests back in his chair.
column6: 他叹了口气，靠回椅背。

column5: And it's starting to weigh down on me.\nLillith, can we talk off the record for a moment?
column6: 而这开始压得我喘不过气。\n莉莉丝，我们能私下聊一会儿吗？

column5: Of course, sir. \nAnytime you'd like.
column6: 当然，先生。\n随时都行。

column5: It's about The Occupation.\nAs you know, I was involved with it.
column6: 是关于“占领”的事。\n你知道的，我曾经参与其中。

column5: Yeah, but that was ages ago.\nIt's all in the past. You're a better man, now.
column6: 是啊，但那是很久以前了。\n都是过去的事了。你现在是个更好的人。

column5: That's the funny thing about the past, Lillith.\nIt always has its way of catching up with you.
column6: 过去这玩意儿就是这样，莉莉丝。\n它总有办法追上你。

column5: What do you mean...?
column6: 你什么意思……？

column5: Honestly, I wouldn't know where to start.\nBut recently, Damek agreed to work with me.\nI wanted exclusive access to Mazeo's spirit idol.
column6: 说实话，我不知该从何说起。\n但最近，达梅克同意与我合作。\n我想要独享马泽奥灵像的进入权。

column5: You lost me...
column6: 我听不懂了……

column5: I want to atone for what I've done, Lillith.\nSo many spirits, trapped in those suits of armor.\nAn eternity of mindless servitude to The Triumvirate.
column6: 我想为我做过的事赎罪，莉莉丝。\n那么多灵，被困在那些盔甲里。\n永无止境、毫无意识地侍奉三人执政团。

column5: And you can fix that with the Spirit Idol?
column6: 而你能用灵像解决这个问题？

column5: I hope so. Part of me always had some doubt.\nBut today — I realized that this is my destiny.\nI can't doubt it, or hide from it any longer.
column6: 但愿如此。我心里一直有点怀疑。\n但今天——我意识到这就是我的宿命。\n我不能再怀疑它，也不能再逃避。

column5: Destiny...?\nI'm not sure I buy into that stuff.\nI'd rather call the shots myself, you know.
column6: 宿命……？\n我不太信这套。\n我更愿意自己做主，你知道的。

column5: Well, maybe {i}purpose{/i} is a better word.\nAt the end of the day, this is still my choice.\nBut I wasn't certain until today. I saw something...
column6: 嗯，也许{i}使命{/i}这个词更合适。\n说到底，这仍是我自己的选择。\n但直到今天我都不确定。我看到了些东西……

column5: What did you see...?
column6: 你看到了什么……？

column5: Back during The Occupation...?\nI killed so many innocent people.\nMade orphans out of so many children.
column6: 当年“占领”的时候……？\n我杀了那么多无辜的人。\n让那么多孩子成了孤儿。

column5: I've been facing that for the last twenty years.\nBut today was the first time I've faced it in person.\nIt's [firstname], and those two companions he had with them.
column6: 这二十年我一直在面对这件事。\n但今天是第一次当面面对。\n是[firstname]，还有跟着他的那两个同伴。

column5: I've been facing that for the last twenty years.\nBut today was the first time I've faced it in person.\nIt's [firstname], and those two companions she had with them.
column6: 这二十年我一直在面对这件事。\n但今天是第一次当面面对。\n是[firstname]，还有跟着她的那两个同伴。

column5: You mean Valessa and Fortaime...?
column6: 你是说瓦莱莎和福泰姆……？

column5: Yes Lillith, all three of them.\nI couldn't put my finger on why they looked familiar.\nBut I just realized it, and I know I need to take action.
column6: 是的，莉莉丝，他们三个都是。\n我一直说不清他们为什么看着眼熟。\n但我刚刚想起来了，我知道我必须采取行动。

column5: He places his head back in his hands, almost ashamed.
column6: 他把头重新埋回双手里，几乎是羞愧难当。

column5: Spitting images of people {i}I{/i} killed during The Occupation.\nI have no doubt in my mind that their parents died by my hand.\nI played a part in condemning them — forcing them into this war.
column6: 活脱脱就是{i}我{/i}在“占领”期间杀掉的那些人的翻版。\n我毫不怀疑，他们的父母死在我手上。\n我也参与了对他们的定罪——把他们逼进了这场战争。

column5: He clenches his fists, trembling as he looks up at Lillith.
column6: 他攥紧拳头，颤抖着抬头看向莉莉丝。

column5: And now I must play my part in ending it.\nI'm going to those tunnels. Right now.
column6: 而现在我必须尽我的一份力，结束这一切。\n我要去那些隧道。现在就去。

column5: Damek sits in a bed, staring down at the pendant I saw him hold back at HQ.{w}\nHe had faced death and came out the other side. That would change {i}any{/i} man.{w}\nBut what happened while he was gone...? That's a question that's been on my mind.
column6: 达梅克坐在床上，低头盯着我在总部见他握过的那个吊坠。{w}\n他曾直面死亡，又从另一边走了出来。那会改变{i}任何{/i}一个人。{w}\n但他不在的那段时间发生了什么……？这个问题一直在我心里。

column5: I approach cautiously, careful not to startle him out of his reverie.{w}\nWhen I get close to him, he looks up at me, making no effort to hide his tears.{w}\nHe finally had time to process everything that happened back in those tunnels.
column6: 我小心翼翼地走近，不惊扰他的沉思。{w}\n当我靠近时，他抬头看我，毫不掩饰自己的泪水。{w}\n他终于有时间去消化隧道里发生的一切。

column5: I was such a fool, [firstname].\nShane tricked me — I was careless.\nI should've never let him get close to me.
column6: 我真是个傻瓜，[firstname]。\n肖恩骗了我——是我大意了。\n我当初就不该让他靠近我。

column5: He knew my weakness, and exploited it.\nIt made me so happy to see him again.\nAnd here I thought I was finally ready...
column6: 他知道我的弱点，还利用了它。\n再见到他让我那么高兴。\n我还以为自己终于准备好了……

column5: Weakness...? What does he mean?
column6: 弱点……？他是什么意思？

column5: Will you have a seat with me, [firstname]?\nI guess I should tell you the truth of what happened.\nFrom the sidelines, I must've looked incompetent.
column6: 能陪我坐会儿吗，[firstname]？\n我想我该告诉你事情的真相。\n从旁人的角度看，我肯定显得很无能。

column5: I mean, I'm trained in combat, you know.\nI should've been able to avoid Shane's dagger with ease.\nIt's what they're all thinking, even if they won't say anything.
column6: 我是说，你懂的，我受过战斗训练。\n我本该轻松避开肖恩的匕首。\n他们心里都是这么想的，只是嘴上不说。

column5: With my interest piqued, I sit down beside Damek.{w}\nHe puts the pendant into one of his pockets, and turns to face me.\nI could tell that his crying spell was over. He was more calm and collected.
column6: 我起了兴趣，在达梅克身旁坐下。{w}\n他把吊坠塞进口袋，转身面对我。\n我能看出他的哭泣已经停了。他平静镇定多了。

column5: Back during the occupation, my parents were killed.\nI saw them murder my Father with no hesitation. Blood everywhere.\nAfter that, my Mother took my hand and tried to find us some shelter.
column6: 当年“占领”的时候，我父母被杀了。\n我眼睁睁看着他们毫不犹豫地杀了我父亲。到处都是血。\n之后，母亲牵着我的手，想找个地方躲藏。

column5: We didn't make it very far. We saw all the bodies in the town square.\nMountains of them. The ground was full of blood, almost like an ocean.\nIf you look closely, you can still see some of the stains, even today.
column6: 我们没走多远。我们看到镇广场上堆满了尸体。\n堆得像山一样。地上全是血，几乎像一片海。\n凑近看的话，即使今天还能看到一些血迹。

column5: This seems unrelated to Shane's attack, but I sit and listen.{w}\nHe told me he'd tell me the \"truth\", so I should see where this goes.
column6: 这似乎和肖恩的袭击无关，但我坐着听下去。{w}\n他说过要告诉我“真相”，我该看看这会通向哪里。

column5: My Mother made a judgment call, and did something risky.\nWhat's the one place they would never look for survivors...?\nThat's right. Amongst the corpses. Covered, and crushed by them.
column6: 母亲做了一个冒险的判断。\n哪里是他们绝不会去找幸存者的地方……？\n没错。就在尸体堆里。被盖住，被压着。

column5: I was crying, but she helped me get underneath a bunch of bodies.\nShe played dead and lay on the outside, holding my hand as tight as she could.\nI remember how she kept telling me that everything would be okay. That soft whisper.
column6: 我在哭，但她帮我钻到一堆尸体下面。\n她装死躺在外侧，尽可能紧地握着我的手。\n我记得她一直告诉我一切都会好的。那轻柔的低语。

column5: Wow...
column6: 天哪……

column5: She didn't make it very long. They found her, and stabbed her over and over.\nI felt her wince every time — the grip on my hand got tighter and tighter.\nThen, after a while, it just let go. I got to feel her final moments.
column6: 她没能撑多久。他们发现了她，一刀又一刀地刺她。\n每一次我都感觉到她抽搐——握着我的手越来越紧。\n然后，过了一会儿，那手松开了。我体会到了她最后的时刻。

column5: The voice telling me that everything would be okay, soon went silent.\nI was left there, underneath a pile of bodies, covered in blood.\nThe last embrace I remember, the last time I held a hand.
column6: 那个告诉我一切都会好的声音，很快就沉默了。\n我被留在那里，压在一堆尸体下面，浑身是血。\n那是我记忆里最后的拥抱，最后一次握住一只手。

column5: It's not something I could ever do again. It just... reminds me of that day.\nNow you understand how Shane made me freeze in fear, and surprise.\nHe was the only other person I told this to. He used that to {i}trick{/i} me.
column6: 这种事我再也做不到了。它只会……让我想起那一天。\n现在你明白肖恩是怎么让我因恐惧和惊愕而僵住的了吧。\n他是我唯一告诉过这件事的人。他利用这点来{i}骗{/i}我。

column5: And he would've killed me too, if it wasn't for you and Howl.\nI was finally ready to get close to somebody again, and then this happens...\nThat's how I know Shane wasn't just acting. He played dirty, and wanted me dead.
column6: 要不是你和豪尔，他也会杀了我。\n我终于准备好再次亲近某个人，然后就出了这种事……\n所以我确定肖恩不只是在演戏。他耍了阴招，想要我死。

column5: There was so much running through my mind the moment he stabbed me.\nI thought perhaps he was trying to win over The Triumvirate, so he could get more intel.\nBut then he stabbed me again, and again. I knew that the man I once knew was gone.
column6: 他刺中我的那一刻，我脑子里闪过无数念头。\n我以为也许他是想取信于三人执政团，好搜集更多情报。\n但他又刺了我一刀，又一刀。我知道我认识的那个人已经不在了。

column5: They did something to him while he was imprisoned. They won him over.\nI don't know how they did it, but they turned him into a completely different person.\nWe must never let another one of our allies fall under their thrall. Never.
column6: 他被囚禁时他们对他做了些什么。他们策反了他。\n我不知道他们是怎么做到的，但他们把他变成了完全另一个人。\n我们绝不能让我方任何一个盟友再落入他们的掌控。绝不能。

column5: I nod, agreeing with Damek.{w}\nBut that was a horrible story.{w}\nGoing through that as a child?
column6: 我点头，赞同达梅克。{w}\n但那是个可怕的故事。{w}\n小时候经历那种事？

column5: His aversion to physical contact makes perfect sense, now.{w}\nAnd Shane is an awful person, having taken advantage of that.{w}\nStartling Damek, making him relive those memories, and killing him.
column6: 现在他排斥身体接触就完全说得通了。{w}\n而肖恩利用这一点，真是个卑鄙的人。{w}\n吓住达梅克，逼他重新经历那些记忆，还想杀了他。

column5: That was despicable.
column6: 太卑鄙了。

column5: Sorry for dropping all of that on you, [firstname].\nI just needed to tell somebody. It was eating away at me.\nAnd I trust you — I know you'd never do anything like Shane did.
column6: 抱歉把这些一股脑倒给你，[firstname]。\n我只是需要找个人说说。它一直在侵蚀我。\n而且我信任你——我知道你绝不会做出肖恩那种事。

column5: That goes without saying.{w}\nHowever, the room soon falls to silence.{w}\nDamek fidgets awkwardly, clearly nervous.
column6: 那还用说。{w}\n然而，房间很快陷入沉默。{w}\n达梅克局促不安地动着，显然很紧张。

column5: Well, I guess that's enough to kill any conversation.\nLike I said, I'm sorry for dropping all of that on you.\nAnything else you need to say to me while you can?
column6: 嗯，我想这足以把任何谈话都聊死了。\n就像我说的，抱歉把这些一股脑倒给你。\n趁还有机会，你还有什么想对我说的吗？

column5: It's easy to say that, but it's harder to actually {i}try{/i}.\nEspecially when you've had a track record like I have.\nI want to — but there's just something stopping me, you know?
column6: 说起来容易，但要真正{i}尝试{/i}就难多了。\n尤其当你有我这样一段经历的时候。\n我想去做——但总有某种东西拦着我，你懂吗？

column5: It's nothing against you, or anyone else I consider a friend.\nI just have to put this barrier up for my own benefit.\nI don't want to hurt anybody either, actually.
column6: 这不是针对你，也不是针对我当作朋友的任何人。\n我只是为了自己才竖起这道屏障。\n其实我也不想伤害任何人。

column5: This is war. I almost died back in the Rebel HQ.\nIf I did — can you imagine the pain my allies would feel?\nGetting close to somebody in a time like this would be a disaster.
column6: 这是战争。我在反抗军总部差点就死了。\n如果我死了——你能想象我的盟友们会有多痛苦吗？\n在这种时候跟人亲近会是一场灾难。

column5: I say nothing, and offer my hand to Damek.{w}\nIn response, he winces, and moves a few inches away.{w}\nI'm not sure what I expected, but it just felt right in the moment.
column6: 我什么也没说，向达梅克伸出手。{w}\n他却一缩，往旁边挪开了几寸。{w}\n我不知道自己期待什么，但那一刻只是觉得该这么做。

column5: I'm sorry, [firstname]...\nI'm just... not ready...
column6: 对不起，[firstname]……\n我只是……还没准备好……

column5: He gulps and gives me a nervous smile.
column6: 他咽了口口水，给了我一个紧张的笑容。

column5: It means a lot though, it really does.\nI just have to put this barrier up for my own benefit.\nI don't want to hurt you either, if that makes any sense.
column6: 不过那对我意义重大，真的。\n我只是为了自己才竖起这道屏障。\n我也不想伤害你，如果这话说得通的话。

column5: This is war. I almost died back in the Rebel HQ.\nIf I did — can you imagine the pain you would feel...?\nGetting close at a time like this could be disastrous.
column6: 这是战争。我在反抗军总部差点就死了。\n如果我死了——你能想象你会有多痛苦吗……？\n在这种时候亲近起来可能会是灾难性的。

column5: Thank you for understanding, [firstname].\nBut I don't need anything more than that — so no sympathy.\nIt was a long time ago, and I just want you to see things differently.
column6: 谢谢你的理解，[firstname]。\n但我不需要更多了——所以别同情我。\n那是很久以前的事，我只希望你能换个角度看事情。

column5: There are those that think I'm incompetent because of what happened.\nBut as long as one person truly understands? Well, that's all I ever need.\nI was uncertain at first, but now I'm not. Telling you was a good idea.
column6: 有人因为发生的事觉得我无能。\n但只要有一个人真正理解？嗯，那我就别无他求了。\n一开始我还不确定，现在不了。告诉你是个好主意。

column5: That's fine, I don't expect you to come up with an entire speech.\nIt's enough to know that you cared to sit through my endless rambling.\nMost people would tell me to shut up, or say that I'm boring them.
column6: 没关系，我不指望你能想出一整篇说辞。\n知道你愿意耐着性子听我没完没了地唠叨，就够了。\n大多数人都会叫我闭嘴，或者说我烦到他们了。

column5: To have the ear of somebody like you? That means a lot.\nNo matter what happens, I hope we can maintain this bond.\nThere's no telling what awaits us in Alarinthia, [firstname].
column6: 能有像你这样的人愿意听我说话？那意义重大。\n无论发生什么，我希望我们能维持这份羁绊。\n阿拉林西亚有什么在等着我们，谁也说不准，[firstname]。

column5: He smiles, and gets out of the bed. I do so as well.{w}\nI could tell that he was ready to end this conversation.
column6: 他笑了笑，下了床。我也跟着起来。{w}\n我能看出他准备好结束这场谈话了。

column5: Well, shall we call it, then?\nI think this is as good a time as any.\nLet that new information process for a while.
column6: 那么，我们就到这儿吧？\n我觉得现在正是时候。\n让那些新信息慢慢消化一阵。

column5: When it comes to my past, that's about it.\nFrom now on, we can look to the future.\nI hope it's just as bright as I picture it.
column6: 关于我的过去，大概就这些了。\n从现在起，我们可以向前看了。\n希望未来和我设想的一样光明。

column5: With that, he walks away from me, and back up to the deck.{w}\nI was glad that he liked me enough to tell me about his past.{w}\nIt was my duty to never take advantage of that — like Shane did.
column6: 说完，他离开我，走回甲板。{w}\n我很高兴他喜欢我到愿意告诉我他的过去。{w}\n我有责任绝不利用这一点——像肖恩那样。

column5: Fortaime paces around the deck of the ship, deep in thought.{w}\nEverything changed over the last few days, so this was insane.{w}\nI hope he's handling it well. I better go and see how he's doing.
column6: 福泰姆在船甲板上踱来踱去，沉思着。{w}\n过去几天一切都变了，这简直疯狂。{w}\n希望他能应对得好。我最好过去看看他怎么样。

column5: Hey there, [firstname].\nThere's something that's been driving me insane.\nYou know how we were all freaking out about Valinorth?
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。\n有件事一直让我快疯了。\n你知道我们之前都为瓦利诺斯急得不行吧？

column5: Without the heat from the spirits, it'd freeze over and die.\nI mean, we believed it — but right now, it doesn't make any sense.\nThe Spirit Realm was a prison, right? Nothing mystical or beneficial.
column6: 没有灵带来的热量，它就会冻住、消亡。\n我是说，我们以前相信这个——但现在想想，根本说不通。\n灵界是个监狱，对吧？没什么神秘，也没什么好处。

column5: It matches up with what people outside of Valinorth were saying.\nWe were just superstitious, and lived in a unique location.\nThe Monarchy gave us visions, and nothing more.
column6: 这和瓦利诺斯之外的人说法一致。\n我们只是迷信，又住在一个特别的地方。\n王室给我们的只是幻象，仅此而已。

column5: We'll have to ask Howl the moment we get the chance.\nIf it's like I think it is, then Valinorth will be fine. No risk at all!\nAs hard as these truths are to believe, they {i}do{/i} have their benefits.
column6: 一有机会我们得问问豪尔。\n如果真像我想的那样，瓦利诺斯就没事。一点风险都没有！\n这些真相再难相信，它们{i}确实{/i}有好处。

column5: In talking to me, he's stopped his pacing, and he looks happy.{w}\nIt's true that a lot of our beliefs were shattered, but that's not a {i}bad{/i} thing.{w}\nA new understanding of the world gave us a new angle to tackle our problems from.
column6: 跟我一说话，他就停下了踱步，看起来很开心。{w}\n我们的许多信念确实破碎了，但那不是件{i}坏{/i}事。{w}\n对世界的新认识给了我们解决问题的全新角度。

column5: At least, it'll make my leadership of Valinorth a lot easier.\nThe one major problem I had to take care of — completely eliminated.\nI couldn't ask for anything better. It's almost like one last gift from the spirits.
column6: 至少，这会让我的瓦利诺斯领导工作轻松许多。\n我必须处理的那个大问题——被彻底消除了。\n再好不过了。简直像是众灵最后的礼物。

column5: At least, it'll make Valessa's job as Elder a lot easier.\nThe one major problem she had to take care of — completely eliminated.\nI know it's stupid to say this now, but it seems like one last gift from the spirits.
column6: 至少，这会让瓦莱莎作为长老的工作轻松许多。\n她必须处理的那个大问题——被彻底消除了。\n我知道现在说这话很蠢，但它像是众灵最后的礼物。

column5: Let's just hope we get lucky like that in Alarinthia.\nSecuring an alliance with barbarians sounds super difficult.\nThey're stubborn in their tradition, just like Valinorth is known to be.
column6: 只希望我们在阿拉林西亚也能这么走运。\n跟蛮族结盟听起来就难如登天。\n他们固守传统，就像瓦利诺斯出了名的那样。

column5: But their tradition isn't steeped in the spirits like ours was.\nAt the end of the day, will they even care about any of this...?\nThey almost live a world away, untouched by our problems.
column6: 但他们的传统不像我们那样浸润着灵。\n说到底，他们会在乎这些吗……？\n他们几乎生活在另一个世界，不受我们问题的波及。

column5: No point worrying about things out of our control, right?\nMaybe we should talk about something we {i}do{/i} have power over.\nRemember that climbing gear Pro gave me money for? Well, check it out!
column6: 担心我们控制不了的事也没用，对吧？\n也许我们该聊聊我们{i}确实{/i}能掌控的事。\n还记得普洛给我钱买的那套攀爬装备吗？看这个！

column5: He wanders over to a bag on the deck, and reaches inside.{w}\nA few moments later, he produces some clawed, metallic objects.{w}\nIt appears that there's one pair for your feet, and one for your hands.
column6: 他晃到甲板上的一个包旁，伸手进去。{w}\n过了一会儿，他掏出一些带爪的金属物件。{w}\n看来一对是给脚的，一对是给手的。

column5: They're adjustable, so you can wear them no matter what!\nYou don't need to look for a foothold anymore, you make them yourself!\nAs long as you're strong enough, there's nothing you can't climb, Monarch.
column6: 它们可以调节，所以你怎么都能戴！\n你不用再找落脚点了，自己就能造出来！\n只要你力气够，没什么是你爬不上去的，君主。

column5: I know what I'm doing as soon as we get back.\nI'm heading to Valinorth, and climbing The Grand Tree!\nI want you to join me. It'll be a good place for you to learn.
column6: 我知道一回去我要做什么。\n我要去瓦利诺斯，爬上巨树！\n我想让你跟我一起。那是个适合你学习的好地方。

column5: I know what you're thinking, though.\n\"Why would I learn to climb on something so difficult?\"\nWell, you have gear now. I never did. It's a {i}huge{/i} advantage.
column6: 不过我知道你在想什么。\n“我为什么要拿这么难爬的东西来练？”\n嗯，你现在有装备了。我以前可没有。那是{i}巨大{/i}的优势。

column5: The only thing holding you back will be your energy.\nBut with everything we've been through, this should be simple.\nI think it'll only take a few hours to climb, if I'm totally honest.
column6: 唯一会拖你后腿的就是体力。\n但经历了我们经历的一切，这应该很简单。\n说实话，我觉得爬上去只要几个小时。

column5: I'll bring us a backpack with a bunch of water.\nOr maybe we should split that over two backpacks.\nDon't want to make one of us carry too much weight.
column6: 我会带一个装满水的背包。\n也许我们该分成两个背包。\n不想让我们其中一个背太重。

column5: He puts the climbing gear back in the bag, clearly excited.{w}\nIt's a breath of fresh air to hear him talk about this stuff so passionately.{w}\nEverybody else is so concerned about the war. It's nice to just push that aside.
column6: 他把攀爬装备放回包里，显然很兴奋。{w}\n听他这么充满热情地聊这些，真是耳目一新。{w}\n其他人都那么担心战争。能把这些搁到一边真好。

column5: Besides, it's a pretty unique date destination, isn't it?\nNot many people can say they've been to the top of The Grand Tree.\nIt's something special. You know, to match how special you are to me.
column6: 再说，这可是个相当独特的约会地点，不是吗？\n没多少人能说自己到过巨树的顶端。\n这是件特别的事。你懂的，正好配得上你对我有多特别。

column5: Anyway, it'll be nice to make some history together.\nNot many people can say they've been to the top of The Grand Tree.\nMaybe we'll start a trend. A sort of, \"coming of age\" thing, you know?
column6: 总之，能一起创造些历史会很好。\n没多少人能说自己到过巨树的顶端。\n也许我们会掀起一股风潮。一种……“成年礼”之类的，你懂吧？

column5: I don't think I've seen him this excited in a long time.{w}\nFor a moment, it feels like all of my worries have simply washed away.{w}\nThey've slipped into the ocean, becoming nothing more than gentle ripples.
column6: 我想我很久没见他这么兴奋过了。{w}\n有那么一刻，感觉我所有的烦恼都被冲刷掉了。{w}\n它们滑入大海，化作不过是温柔的涟漪。

column5: Fortaime starts to walk around the ship again, and stretch his body.{w}\nIt's almost like he was preparing for the marathon of a lifetime.{w}\nOf course, this had been a life long dream of his, after all.
column6: 福泰姆又开始在船上走动，伸展身体。{w}\n简直像在为一生一次的马拉松做准备。{w}\n当然，毕竟这是他毕生的梦想。

column5: I know there's so much danger in our future.\nBut there's happiness too, you know?\nLots to look forward to in the end.
column6: 我知道我们的未来充满危险。\n但也有快乐，你知道吗？\n到最后，有很多值得期待的东西。

column5: Besides, I doubt I'll be key to our Alarinthian alliance.\nSo in the meantime, there's not really anything else I can do.\nI've been practicing my climbing on the netting of the ship.
column6: 再说，我估计在阿拉林西亚结盟这事上我起不了关键作用。\n所以在那之前，我其实也没什么别的能做的。\n我一直在船上的网绳上练习攀爬。

column5: People are worried that I'll fall off, but I tell them not to worry.\nIt's very rare that I fall off, and I usually shake it off pretty quickly.\nI saw some of them get together and make some betting pools.
column6: 大家担心我会摔下来，但我叫他们别担心。\n我很少摔下来，而且通常很快就没事了。\n我看见他们几个人凑在一起开了赌局。

column5: It's a pretty boring voyage, so they make their own entertainment.\nI suddenly start to know why pirates enjoy fighting and gambling so much.\nWhen you're out at sea, there's just nothing much to do. It's pretty crazy.
column6: 这趟航行挺无聊的，所以他们就自娱自乐。\n我突然开始明白海盗为什么那么喜欢打架和赌博了。\n在海上，实在没什么事可做。真够疯的。

column5: I'd go insane if I were a pirate — I just know it.\nAfter this war, I think I want to settle down on the mainland.\nSailing isn't for me. I can say that with absolute certainty.
column6: 我要是海盗肯定会疯掉——我敢肯定。\n这场战争之后，我想在大陆上安顿下来。\n航海不适合我。这我可以百分之百肯定。

column5: I'm not sure this life is for me, either. It's just different.{w}\nValinorth was a completely different atmosphere than any of this.{w}\nEven Mazeo was a bit of a culture shock to me and my friends.
column6: 我也不确定这种生活适合我。只是很不一样。{w}\n瓦利诺斯的氛围和这一切截然不同。{w}\n就连马泽奥对我和我朋友来说都有点文化冲击。

column5: I can't even imagine what Alarinthia and Balteus will be like.{w}\nI look off to the horizon. We must still be pretty far away.{w}\nThere's no sight of land ahead. How much farther to go...?
column6: 我甚至想象不出阿拉林西亚和巴尔泰乌斯会是什么样。{w}\n我望向地平线。我们肯定还离得很远。{w}\n前方看不到陆地的影子。还要走多远……？

column5: Sorry for rambling on, but yeah, there's nothing else to do.\nI bet the other people will be able to keep your interest longer.\nBut before you go, I have just {i}one{/i} question to ask you.
column6: 抱歉我一直在唠叨，不过是啊，也没别的事可做。\n我敢打赌其他人能让你更久地提起兴趣。\n但你走之前，我只想问你{i}一个{/i}问题。

column5: He stops stretching and walks right up to me, with a sly smirk.
column6: 他停止伸展，带着狡黠的坏笑径直走到我面前。

column5: Do we make it to the top, or do we fail...?\nWhat's your bet, [firstname]? And {i}no{/i} refusing.\nWe're on a pirate ship, so we need to act like Pirates.
column6: 我们登顶，还是失败……？\n你押哪个，[firstname]？而且{i}不许{/i}拒绝。\n我们在海盗船上，就得像海盗一样行事。

column5: Optimism? I love it! \nThe other pirates didn't share that trait.\nThey seemed to actually look forward to failure.
column6: 乐观？我喜欢！\n别的海盗可没这特质。\n他们好像还真盼着我失败。

column5: Though I guess that would be fun to watch.\nCan you imagine if I fell off the netting into the sea?\nThey'd probably stand by and laugh, rather than help.
column6: 不过我猜那看着可能挺有意思。\n你能想象我从网绳上掉进海里吗？\n他们大概会站在一旁笑，而不是来帮忙。

column5: Realism, huh? I can accept that.\nAt least you didn't bet that we'd fall.\nIf you did, I'd be upset at your confidence.
column6: 现实主义，是吧？我能接受。\n至少你没押我们会失败。\n如果你真押了，我会对你的“信心”感到不满。

column5: Remember who your Master is, [firstname].\nYou're an Apprentice to the best, so I bet we'll make it.\nNow we just need to decide what the stakes are.
column6: 记住你的师父是谁，[firstname]。\n你是最棒的师父的学徒，所以我押我们会成功。\n现在只差定下赌注了。

column5: Hmm...
Oh, I know! A kiss.\nLoser has to kiss the winner.\nAnd yes — I {i}totally{/i} rigged it.
column6: 哦，有了！一个吻。\n输的人要亲赢的人。\n没错——我{i}绝对{/i}作弊了。

column5: This way — I win no matter what.
column6: 这样一来——不管怎样都是我赢。

column5: I guess we can figure that out when the time comes.\nWhich, as I'm starting to realize, is pretty darn soon.\nThink of some ideas in your off time, alright?
column6: 我想到时候再定也行。\n而我开始意识到，那时候来得还挺快。\n空闲的时候想想点子，好吗？

column5: We'll announce the terms before we climb.
column6: 我们在攀爬前宣布赌注条件。

column5: With a smirk and a wink, he quickly runs off on his way.{w}\nFull of energy, it seems. Or perhaps he's going stir-crazy.{w}\nI don't blame him, being stuck at sea with nothing else to do.
column6: 他坏笑一下，眨眨眼，很快跑开去了。{w}\n看来精力充沛。又或者他是关疯了。{w}\n我不怪他，困在海上无事可做。

column5: I guess our goal was clear. We'd climb The Grand Tree.{w}\nThat is, if we even made it back from Alarinthia in one piece.{w}\nHis ability to focus on the positive stuff during war is admirable.
column6: 我想我们的目标清楚了。我们要爬上巨树。{w}\n前提是我们能从阿拉林西亚完好无损地回来。{w}\n他在战时还能专注于积极的东西，令人钦佩。

column5: Admirable, if not a bit naive. Hopefully I could join in his positivity.{w}\nBut this blade on my back, both literally and figuratively weighs me down.{w}\nI might leave it on the surface when we climb. Yeah, that would make things easier.
column6: 令人钦佩，哪怕有点天真。希望我也能加入他的乐观。{w}\n但我背上这把剑，无论字面上还是比喻上都压着我。{w}\n攀爬时我或许可以把它留在地面。嗯，那会让事情轻松些。

column5: A lot easier.
column6: 轻松得多。

column5: Fortaime's loyalty scene is now available when you return to the mainland.{w}\nThe game will notify you when you have access to the loyalty scene system.{w}\nLoyalty scenes can be initiated by clicking that character at the War Table.
column6: 返回大陆后，福泰姆的忠诚剧情将解锁。{w}\n当你可以使用忠诚剧情系统时，游戏会通知你。{w}\n在战争桌面上点击该角色即可触发忠诚剧情。

column5: I make my way down to the ship cabin, and see Ulric sitting on a bed.{w}\nAt least, whatever passes for a bed aboard a somewhat cramped ship.{w}\nHe's sharpening his sword, clearly exerting himself as he does so.
column6: 我下到船舱，看见乌尔里克坐在一张床上。{w}\n至少，是在这艘有点拥挤的船上勉强算床的东西。{w}\n他正在磨剑，动作间显然很用力。

column5: Hey there, [firstname].\nAs you can see, I'm getting ready for combat.\nI give it two days before we're dragged into conflict.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。\n如你所见，我在为战斗做准备。\n我估计不出两天我们就会被卷进冲突。

column5: They don't use words to resolve things in Alarinthia.\nIt's always a duel, or a tournament. That's all they do.\nWhen we're there, we might as well speak their language.
column6: 在阿拉林西亚，他们不用言语解决问题。\n总是决斗，或者比武大会。他们就干这些。\n到了那儿，我们不妨入乡随俗。

column5: He smirks, as if the promise of action is exciting to him.{w}\nHe did hate Alarinthia, but he also loved combat. It was his nature.{w}\nHopefully he'd get to tackle a challenge worthy of his skill while we were there.
column6: 他坏笑一下，仿佛有仗可打就让他兴奋。{w}\n他确实讨厌阿拉林西亚，但他也热爱战斗。那是他的天性。{w}\n希望我们在那儿的时候，他能遇到配得上他身手的挑战。

column5: Gotta make the most of a bad situation, right?\nI'll get to give my sword arm a real challenge.\nWhat about you, [firstname]? Excited for this?
column6: 逆境也得尽量利用，对吧？\n我这条舞剑的手臂，可算能迎来一场真正的挑战了。\n你呢，[firstname]？期待吗？

column5: That's the spirit. We're going to make history.\nI really hope we can help Vivien, and change the nation.\nAs you know, that's been my dream for the longest time.
column6: 这才对。我们要创造历史。\n我真的很希望能帮到薇薇安，改变这个国家。\n如你所知，这是我长久以来的梦想。

column5: It's nice to know that her movement actually has some traction.\nIf only my parents were so lucky. I bet they'd be proud, [firstname].\nThe foe may seem impossible to beat, but I have a feeling we can do it.
column6: 知道她的运动真的有些进展，真好。\n要是我父母也这么幸运就好了。我打赌他们会骄傲的，[firstname]。\n敌人看似不可战胜，但我有预感我们能做到。

column5: That is, if we even get the opportunity to side with Vivien.\nIf we get stuck with Draycu, I have to admit that I'll be disappointed.\nWe'd get our alliance, but at the end of the day, Alarinthia would be the same.
column6: 前提是我们真有机会站在薇薇安这边。\n如果被迫和德雷库合作，我得承认我会失望。\n我们能拿到盟约，但说到底，阿拉林西亚还是老样子。

column5: Glad to hear. I like that in a partner.\nMaking change {i}together{/i} — now that's amazing.\nNot everybody would be so brave, you know.
column6: 很高兴听你这么说。我喜欢搭档有这股劲。\n{i}一起{/i}做出改变——那可太棒了。\n不是每个人都有这份勇气，你知道的。

column5: It's almost overwhelming to think about, actually.\nI have the support of The Monarch of Alestia...?\nThere's almost nothing we can't accomplish now.
column6: 说实话，想到这个几乎让人承受不住。\n我有了阿莱斯蒂亚君主的支持……？\n现在几乎没有我们做不到的事。

column5: Reminds me of myself when I was younger.\nJust be careful, [firstname]. Don't make reckless decisions.\nAfter this war is over, you have an entire world to rule over, you know.
column6: 让我想起年轻时的自己。\n小心点，[firstname]。别做鲁莽的决定。\n这场战争结束后，你有一整个世界要统治，你知道的。

column5: Not to put any pressure on you, of course. Actually, it's the opposite.\nKnowing your importance should fill you with hope and resolve.\nWith your authority, and that blade — you can do anything.
column6: 当然，不是要给你压力。其实正相反。\n知道自己的重要性应该让你充满希望和决心。\n凭你的权威，还有那把剑——你无所不能。

column5: Sometime it's necessary — you can't avoid it.\nEspecially with what happened back at the Rebel HQ.\nDo you think we could've responded with a warm hug...?
column6: 有时这是必要的——你躲不掉。\n尤其考虑到反抗军总部发生的事。\n你觉得我们能用温暖的拥抱来回应吗……？

column5: Do you think words could've stopped their assault?\nNo. It's foolish to think that, but it's an admirable dream to have.\nMaybe after this war, in the new world, we can resolve things peacefully.
column6: 你觉得言语能阻止他们的进攻吗？\n不能。这么想很愚蠢，但有这样的梦想令人钦佩。\n也许这场战争之后，在新世界里，我们能和平解决问题。

column5: But not while we're under The Triumvirate's thumb. Not at all.\nThey only know war. They kill and they steal to get what they want.\nUntil we're in power, all we can do is respond to them in kind.
column6: 但只要我们在三人执政团的压制下就不行。完全不行。\n他们只懂战争。为了得到想要的，他们杀人、抢夺。\n在我们掌权之前，我们能做的只是以牙还牙。

column5: Yeah, I guess this stuff isn't for everybody.\nFor me, though? It's a source of excitement.\nNothing gets my blood pumping faster than a fight.
column6: 是啊，我想这种事不是人人都受得了。\n但对我来说？它是兴奋的来源。\n没什么比一场战斗更能让我热血沸腾了。

column5: Facing death, and then coming out alive?\nI almost can't describe it. It's truly amazing.\nWe look our end in the eyes, and say \"No\".
column6: 直面死亡，然后活着走出来？\n我几乎无法形容。那真是不可思议。\n我们直视自己的终结，说“不”。

column5: But I'm guessing you didn't come down here for a lecture.\nHave a seat. There's something I'd like to talk to you about.
column6: 不过我猜你下来不是为了听我说教。\n坐吧。有件事我想跟你聊聊。

column5: I nod, and sit down beside him.{w}\nHe slowly rests his hand on top of mine, and holds it.{w}\nSo much had happened since the last time we were together.
column6: 我点头，在他身旁坐下。{w}\n他慢慢把手覆在我的手上，握住。{w}\n自从上次我们在一起之后，发生了太多事。

column5: I nod, and sit down beside him.{w}\nHe continues sharpening his sword, and I watch.{w}\nIt must've gotten worn out during the battle back at HQ.
column6: 我点头，在他身旁坐下。{w}\n他继续磨剑，我看着。{w}\n它肯定在总部的战斗中磨损了。

column5: I don't want to scare you, and I'm not really hiding anything.\nBut we're about to go to my homeland. You might... hear things.\nCan you promise me something, Monarch? No matter what happens?
column6: 我不想吓你，我也没真的隐瞒什么。\n但我们要去我的故乡了。你也许会……听到些事。\n能答应我一件事吗，君主？无论发生什么？

column5: Remember me for the things I've done for {i}you{/i}, and The Rebellion.\nNo matter what you hear about me, or my past? Please don't judge me.\nI wouldn't judge you based on your past, so I expect the same from you.
column6: 记住我为你{i}和{/i}反抗军做过的事。\n不管你听到关于我或我过去的什么？请别评判我。\n我不会因为你的过去评判你，所以我也期望你能同样对我。

column5: I nod. I can afford him that courtesy, as long as he's not hiding anything heinous.{w}\nBut he doesn't seem like the type. He's truly devoted his life to the same cause as me.
column6: 我点头。只要他没有隐瞒什么穷凶极恶的事，这份礼遇我可以给他。{w}\n但他不像是那种人。他确实把一生献给了和我相同的事业。

column5: Good. Then that's pretty much everything I had to say.\nI was really worried. I wasn't sure how to handle that topic.\nSo — rather than overthinking it, I just shot straight. Thank you.
column6: 好。那差不多就是我要说的全部了。\n我一直很担心。我不知道该怎么处理这个话题。\n所以——与其想太多，我干脆直说。谢谢你。

column5: It was especially hard since we're kind of \"involved\", now.\nIs that the right word for what we are? I don't really know.\nAfter what we did back in Mazeo, I think it's a safe term.
column6: 尤其难开口，因为我们现在算是“有牵连”了。\n这个词形容我们合适吗？我也不太清楚。\n鉴于我们在马泽奥做过的事，我想这说法还算稳妥。

column5: I don't want to complicate things, so I'll just be quiet.\nBut don't think I've forgotten about what happened.\nIf we get the time, I'd like for it to happen again...
column6: 我不想把事情弄复杂，所以我就闭嘴了。\n但别以为我忘了发生的事。\n如果有机会，我希望还能再来一次……

column5: But I doubt we'll be able to do that on this ship.\nYou can't even breathe without someone else hearing it.\nI have my ways of keeping quiet, but I wouldn't want to get caught.
column6: 但我估计在这艘船上我们做不了。\n你连喘口气都会被人听见。\n我有办法保持安静，但我不想被抓个正着。

column5: It was especially hard, since you're such a powerful figure.\nI'd hate to get on your bad side, so I need to be fully open.\nI have a few secrets, as we all do — but nothing really bad.
column6: 尤其难开口，因为你是这么有权势的人物。\n我可不想惹你不高兴，所以我得完全坦诚。\n我有几个秘密，人人都有——但没什么真正糟糕的。

column5: If you don't find out in Alarinthia, I'll probably tell you myself.\nIn fact, maybe it would mean more if it came directly from me.\nSorry — I must sound stupid. I'm not really good at this kind of stuff.
column6: 如果你在阿拉林西亚没发现，我大概会自己告诉你。\n其实，也许由我亲口说出来会更有意义。\n抱歉——我听起来肯定很蠢。我实在不擅长这些。

column5: Talking about myself is hard. It definitely helps to get drunk.\nBut ale was something they {i}didn't{/i} think to pack for this voyage.\nMaybe I'll pull some strings so the ride back can be more \"lively\".
column6: 谈自己很难。喝醉肯定有帮助。\n但这次航行他们{i}没{/i}想着带上麦酒。\n也许我会动用点关系，让回程更“热闹”些。

column5: He gives me another one of those trademark smirks.{w}\nI get the feeling that he really does use alcohol as a social crutch.{w}\nHe's much more open and lively while under the influence. Is that bad?
column6: 他又给了我一个标志性的坏笑。{w}\n我感觉他确实把酒精当作社交的拐杖。{w}\n他在酒意上头时开放活泼得多。这算坏事吗？

column5: I guess it's not my place to say. As long as it doesn't get in the way of his duty.{w}\nSomething told me that our visit to Alarinthia would put him in the spotlight more than ever.{w}\nI get up from the bed, and turn around to face him. He continues working his sword.
column6: 我想轮不到我来说。只要不碍他的职责就好。{w}\n我总觉得我们去阿拉林西亚会让他比以往更受瞩目。{w}\n我从床上起身，转身面对他。他继续弄着他的剑。

column5: Sorry I didn't have much to say. I guess I'm a little shy.\nBut it'll all make sense in time. I can promise you that.\nWhen that time comes — you need to keep your promise.
column6: 抱歉我没多少话说。我想我有点害羞。\n但到时候一切都会明白的。这我可以向你保证。\n到那时候——你得遵守你的承诺。

column5: He's really pushing this promise thing. Should I be concerned...?{w}\nI'd hate for him to use it as leverage if some horrible secret came to light.{w}\nThankfully, I see Ulric as a good person. He wouldn't hide anything bad from us.
column6: 他真的很强调这个承诺。我该担心吗……？{w}\n我不想万一有什么可怕的秘密曝光，他拿这个当筹码。{w}\n幸好，我认为乌尔里克是个好人。他不会对我们隐瞒什么坏事。

column5: Like he said, it'll all make sense in time.{w}\nAll I can really do, is go about my business and wait.{w}\nToo bad there wasn't enough privacy to have some more fun.
column6: 就像他说的，到时候一切都会明白。{w}\n我真正能做的，就是照常做事，等待。{w}\n可惜不够私密，没法再多找点乐子。

column5: Something told me we'd make up for that next time we had the chance.
column6: 我总觉得下次有机会我们会补回来。

column5: Like he said, it'll all make sense in time.{w}\nAll I can really do, is go about my business and wait.{w}\nSuddenly, I'm more excited about our journey to Alarinthia.
column6: 就像他说的，到时候一切都会明白。{w}\n我真正能做的，就是照常做事，等待。{w}\n突然间，我对我们前往阿拉林西亚的旅程更期待了。

column5: Both Alestia, and my comrades, were slowly opening up to me.{w}\nIn the last few days, everything had changed. What else would change?\nThat thought fills me with both excitement and fright at the same time.
column6: 阿莱斯蒂亚和我的同伴们，都在慢慢向我敞开心扉。{w}\n过去几天，一切都变了。还会有什么改变？\n这个念头让我既兴奋又恐惧。

column5: I step toward Valessa, who has her hands on the ship's railing.{w}\nShe seems lost in thought, but who wouldn't be after recent events?{w}\nCareful not to startle her, I simply stand beside her, and rest my hands too.
column6: 我走向瓦莱莎，她双手扶着船舷栏杆。{w}\n她似乎陷入沉思，但最近出了这些事，谁不会呢？{w}\n我小心不惊扰她，只是站到她身旁，也把手搭上去。

column5: You know, for once, I thought things were going well.\nWe had an army, and it seemed like our objective was clear.\nBut they outsmarted us. They caught us off guard. We were careless.
column6: 你知道吗，难得有一回，我以为事情进展顺利。\n我们有了一支军队，目标似乎也很明确。\n但他们比我们更狡猾。他们打了我们一个措手不及。是我们大意了。

column5: They always say to be cautious if things are going too well.\nEspecially in war. We got blinded by the victory we thought we secured.\nNobody thought to question our course of action, or Damek's orders.
column6: 人们总说，事情太顺利时就要当心。\n尤其在战争中。我们被自以为到手的胜利蒙蔽了双眼。\n没人想过去质疑我们的行动方针，或者达梅克的命令。

column5: And I'm supposed to be the next Elder of Valinorth...\nFor the safety of our nation, I need to be {i}better{/i} than this.\nI need to plan for every course of action, however unlikely.
column6: 而我还应该是瓦利诺斯的下一任长老……\n为了我们国家的安全，我必须{i}做得更好{/i}。\n我需要对每一种可能，无论多不可能的走向都做好打算。

column5: And to top it all off, you don't need a Scribe anymore.\nFortaime gets to lead our nation, and I'm left with nothing...?\nThat's hardly fair. Now I have no idea what to do with myself.
column6: 更糟的是，你不再需要书记官了。\n福泰姆将领导我们的国家，而我什么都没剩下……？\n这太不公平了。现在我都不知道自己该做什么。

column5: I just wish things could be clear, like they used to be.\nThough things were difficult, our future was certain.\nWe don't even know if we can secure this alliance.
column6: 我只是希望事情能像从前那样清楚。\n虽然艰难，但我们的未来是确定的。\n现在我们连能不能拿到这个盟约都不知道。

column5: I want to believe you, but I'm just not sure.\nWe thought things would work out back at the Rebel HQ.\nLook how that turned out, [firstname]. We were reckless.
column6: 我想相信你，但我就是不确定。\n在反抗军总部时我们也以为事情会顺利。\n看看结果如何，[firstname]。我们太鲁莽了。

column5: I don't want to sound mean, but I don't share those thoughts.\nIt's important to take a step back, and look at the big picture.\nThat way you don't get blinded, and act based on your ego.
column6: 我不想显得刻薄，但我不认同那些想法。\n退一步看全局很重要。\n这样你才不会蒙蔽，不会凭自尊行事。

column5: Really...? Are you sure about that, [firstname].\nYou have a world to save. You can't just focus on {i}me{/i}.\nAnother mistake would mean the end of our cause — permanently.
column6: 真的……？你确定吗，[firstname]。\n你有一整个世界要拯救。你不能只盯着{i}我{/i}。\n再犯一次错，就意味着我们的事业彻底终结。

column5: I mean, that's why I haven't really had time to think about romance.\nWhat good is planning my future, if I might not even be alive next week?\nThat would just lead to heartbreak. Heartbreak could be catastrophic.
column6: 我是说，这就是我一直没时间考虑感情的原因。\n如果我下周可能就死了，规划未来又有什么意义？\n那只会带来心碎。而心碎可能是灾难性的。

column5: Normally, hearing you say that would fill me with fright.\nBut right now? It's important to know that I'm not alone.\nI'm not the only one who feels this way. That's good.
column6: 换作平时，听你这么说会让我害怕。\n但现在？知道我不是一个人很重要。\n不是只有我这么想。这很好。

column5: It's not easy, having your whole belief system destroyed.\nIf I'm honest, I kind of wish I never got thrust into this mess.\nLiving in ignorance, just like everybody else. What a dream.
column6: 整套信仰体系被摧毁，这可不容易。\n说实话，我有点希望自己从没被扔进这摊烂事里。\n像其他人一样活在无知中。多美好啊。

column5: After this war is over, we'll have to tell {i}them{/i} the truth, too.\nDo you think they'll even believe the truth of the spirit realm?\nI mean, do {i}I{/i} even believe it? Part of me still feels doubt.
column6: 这场战争结束后，我们也得告诉{i}他们{/i}真相。\n你觉得他们会相信灵界的真相吗？\n我是说，{i}我{/i}自己相信吗？我心里还是有疑虑。

column5: Heh. Still have time for that sense of humor, huh?\nHonestly, that's a little relieving. Thanks for the laugh.\nIt's been so long, I've forgotten what smiling feels like.
column6: 呵。还有工夫开玩笑，是吧？\n说实话，这让人稍微松了口气。谢谢你逗我笑。\n太久了，我都忘了笑是什么感觉。

column5: Thanks, [firstname]. It helps to know that. It really does.\nWe always assume that we're alone in our struggles, you know?\nSometimes opening up can do wonders. Especially to you, it seems.
column6: 谢谢，[firstname]。知道这一点很有帮助。真的。\n我们总以为自己的挣扎是孤独的，你知道吗？\n有时候敞开心扉会有奇效。看来对你尤其如此。

column5: I guess it's safe to assume that everybody is shaken up right now.\nMaybe I'll go talk to a few other rebels after this, and cheer them up.\nKnowing you're not alone helps a lot. Maybe they need a quick reminder.
column6: 我想可以肯定，现在每个人都很受震动。\n也许这事之后我去找几个反抗军聊聊，给他们打打气。\n知道你不是一个人很有帮助。也许他们需要有人提醒一下。

column5: She lets out a loud sigh as we stare off into the horizon.{w}\nThe slow rocking of the ship pushes us closer together.{w}\nWith the distance closed, I can hear her more clearly.
column6: 我们望着地平线，她重重叹了口气。{w}\n船身缓慢的摇晃把我们推得更近。{w}\n距离拉近了，我能更清楚地听见她。

column5: There's definitely more on her mind, I can tell.{w}\nBut I can't force her to open up, so I stand there in silence.{w}\nMy ears are open to her, as long as she decides to speak.
column6: 我能看出她心里肯定还有别的事。{w}\n但我不能逼她开口，所以我默默站着。{w}\n只要她愿意说，我的耳朵为她敞开。

column5: I was so lost in thought, I couldn't sleep last night.\nI decided to help Alex prepare the ship for our voyage.\nWe got to talking, and he told me something shocking...
column6: 昨晚我思绪万千，睡不着。\n我决定帮亚历克斯准备出航的船。\n我们聊了起来，他告诉了我一件震惊的事……

column5: I was so lost in thought, I couldn't sleep last night.\nI decided to help Nada prepare the ship for our voyage.\nWe got to talking, and she told me something shocking...
column6: 昨晚我思绪万千，睡不着。\n我决定帮娜达准备出航的船。\n我们聊了起来，她告诉了我一件震惊的事……

column5: I'm not even sure if I should tell you this, [firstname].\nBut I guess it's something you deserve to know.\nRemember how those people recognized us?
column6: 我甚至不确定该不该告诉你这个，[firstname]。\n但我想这是你该知道的事。\n记得那些人认出我们了吗？

column5: She must be talking about Gryz and Grayson.{w}\nThey both recognized us when we first met.
column6: 她说的肯定是格瑞兹和格雷森。{w}\n我们初次见面时他们都认出了我们。

column5: They recognized us too. Immediately.\nI assumed it's because they knew our parents.\nBut then they told me {i}how{/i} they knew them.
column6: 他们也认出了我们。立刻就认出来了。\n我以为是因为他们认识我们的父母。\n但后来他们告诉了我，他们{i}怎么{/i}认识他们的。

column5: She closes her eyes, and looks up to the sky.
column6: 她闭上眼，抬头望向天空。

column5: Our parents were pirates, [firstname].\nFeared, hated, {i}legendary{/i} pirates.\nSure explains their \"trips\" to Mazeo.
column6: 我们的父母是海盗，[firstname]。\n令人畏惧、遭人憎恨的{i}传奇{/i}海盗。\n这就解释了他们的马泽奥“旅行”。

column5: At first I didn't believe it. I was lost in denial.\nBut they kept telling me more and more, and I had to accept it.\nI always pictured our parents as these perfect, untarnished people.
column6: 一开始我不信。我沉浸在否认中。\n但他们越说越多，我不得不接受。\n我一直把我们的父母想象成完美无瑕的人。

column5: But they were killers. They broke the law. They pillaged.\nThey were part of the reason The Triumvirate launched The Occupation.\nI know what you're going to say. \"They wanted the idol\". Piracy was a cover.
column6: 但他们是杀人犯。他们违法。他们掠夺。\n他们是三人执政团发动“占领”的原因之一。\n我知道你要说什么。“他们想要偶像”。海盗只是幌子。

column5: And while you may be right, the excuse was still valid.\nAt the end of the day, piracy was running rampant throughout Mazeo.\nOur parents played a part in giving them this perfect excuse, don't you see?
column6: 就算你说得对，那个借口依然成立。\n说到底，海盗行为在马泽奥肆虐。\n我们的父母也参与了，给了他们这个完美的借口，你明白吗？

column5: And in doing so, they are partly responsible for all of those deaths.\nWe always thought they were innocent victims. But were they really?\nHonestly, I doubt I'll be doing much sleep tonight either, [firstname].
column6: 也正因如此，他们对那些死亡负有部分责任。\n我们一直以为他们是无辜的受害者。但真的是吗？\n说实话，我估计今晚我也睡不着，[firstname]。

column5: She lets out another sigh, even more exasperated than the last one.
column6: 她又叹了口气，比刚才那声更加无奈。

column5: Let's sum it up, shall we?
column6: 我们来总结一下，好吗？

column5: There's no more spirit realm. Our belief system was shattered.\nAlmost the entire Rebellion was killed in action. We were tricked.\nAnd to top it all off, I'm the daughter of some ruthless pirate killers?
column6: 灵界没了。我们的信仰体系碎了。\n几乎整个反抗军都阵亡了。我们被骗了。\n更糟的是，我还是几个残暴海盗杀手的女儿？

column5: How am I supposed to process all of this? How will {i}you{/i}?\nYour parents, my parents, Fortaime's parents... All six of them.\nThey're not the people we thought they were. What do we do...?
column6: 我该怎么消化这一切？{i}你{/i}又该怎么消化？\n你的父母，我的父母，福泰姆的父母……六个人。\n他们不是我们以为的那种人。我们该怎么办……？

column5: She nods, without offering a reply of her own.{w}\nBut I know she understands. This doesn't change much.{w}\nThe goals, and the journey ahead of us, would remain the same.
column6: 她点点头，没有自己作答。{w}\n但我知道她明白。这改变不了多少。{w}\n目标，还有我们前方的旅程，都不会变。

column5: Without saying anything, I step closer, and hold her hand.{w}\nShe grips it tightly, as they both rest on the wooden rails of the ship.{w}\nMoments later, however, she takes a few steps closer to me.
column6: 我什么也没说，走近一步，握住她的手。{w}\n当两只手都搭在船的木质栏杆上时，她紧紧握住。{w}\n然而片刻之后，她朝我走近了几步。

column5: Placing her head on my shoulder, she wraps her free arm around mine.{w}\nHugging it tightly, I can feel her tremble, as emotion wells up within her.{w}\nHow she feels is understandable. She's going through so much right now.
column6: 她把头靠在我肩上，用空着的手臂环住我的胳膊。{w}\n她紧紧抱着，我能感觉到她颤抖，情绪在她心中涌起。{w}\n她的感受可以理解。她现在承受着太多。

column5: She scoffs, not even giving me a reply of her own.{w}\nBut I know she understands. This doesn't change much.\nThe goals, and the journey ahead of us, would remain the same.
column6: 她嗤笑一声，甚至没有自己作答。{w}\n但我知道她明白。这改变不了多少。\n目标，还有我们前方的旅程，都不会变。

column5: She nods, without offering a reply of her own.{w}\nBut I know she understands. This doesn't change much.{w}\nThe goals, and the journey ahead of us, would remain the same.
column6: 她点点头，没有自己作答。{w}\n但我知道她明白。这改变不了多少。{w}\n目标，还有我们前方的旅程，都不会变。

column5: I'm just so lost, [firstname]...
column6: 我只是好迷茫，[firstname]……

column5: Honestly, part of me feels the same way.{w}\nIn that moment, there's nothing left to say.{w}\nWe stare off into the ocean. Together.
column6: 说实话，我也有点同感。{w}\n那一刻，再没什么可说的了。{w}\n我们望着大海。一起。

column5: This was a turning point in all of our lives.{w}\nHow we handled things would define who we became.{w}\nOur conversation ends with that thought, bringing both hope and despair.
column6: 这是我们所有人生命中的一个转折点。{w}\n我们如何处理事情，将决定我们成为什么样的人。{w}\n我们的谈话就在这个念头中结束，既带来希望，也带来绝望。

column5: I see Pro sitting at one of the beds, striking a match.{w}\nHe uses it to light some nearby candles, creating a laid back atmosphere.{w}\nThe candle slowly fills the crew quarters with a sweet aroma. Very relaxing.
column6: 我看见普洛坐在一张床边，擦燃一根火柴。{w}\n他用它点燃旁边的几支蜡烛，营造出悠闲的氛围。{w}\n蜡烛慢慢让船员舱充满甜美的香气。非常放松。

column5: Hey there, [firstname].\nPerfect timing, actually.\nI wanted to talk to you.
column6: 嘿，[firstname]。\n其实来得正好。\n我正想跟你聊聊。

column5: We were supposed to have a date, right?\nI mean — we wanted to see if we click, or whatever.\nI'm glad we decided to start slow, without making mistakes.
column6: 我们本该约会的，对吧？\n我是说——我们想看看合不合得来，之类的。\n我很高兴我们决定慢慢来，不犯错。

column5: I thought we could get to know each other a little better.\nUnfortunately, our time was cut short back at the Rebel HQ.\nBut this a long voyage, with no need to cut any corners.
column6: 我想我们可以多了解一下彼此。\n可惜在反抗军总部时，我们的时间被打断了。\n但这是趟漫长的航行，不必走捷径。

column5: So, wanna have a seat? We can get things started.\nThe candles are supposed to be relaxing. Something about aromatherapy.\nI never really looked into it, but I'm scared of water — so I needed help.
column6: 那么，想坐下吗？我们可以开始。\n这些蜡烛应该能让人放松。好像是芳香疗法之类的。\n我从没认真研究过，但我怕水——所以我需要点帮助。

column5: I sit down beside Pro on the bed, already one fact richer.{w}\nSo he was scared of water? He must not be having much fun.{w}\nIt makes me wonder what else I don't know about him. He's a mystery.
column6: 我在床边普洛身旁坐下，已经多知道了一件事。{w}\n原来他怕水？那他肯定没怎么享受。{w}\n这让我好奇还有多少关于他的事我不知道。他是个谜。

column5: You should tell me about yourself, [firstname].\nAnd this is because I'm genuinely interested, I swear.\nWhatever you tell me — I'll never write down in any books.
column6: 你该跟我讲讲你自己，[firstname]。\n这是因为我真心感兴趣，我发誓。\n无论你告诉我什么——我都绝不会写进任何书里。

column5: That's what friends do, right? Confide in each other?\nI know I always talk about writing books, and conducting interviews.\nBut the truth is, this time — I want to keep things between the two of us.
column6: 朋友就是这样，对吧？互相倾诉？\n我知道我总是说要写书、做访谈。\n但说实话，这一次——我想让事情只留在我们俩之间。

column5: I nod, and tell him a random fact about myself. Nothing harmful, just small.{w}\nHe smiles, and we start to exchange facts about each other. He seems really happy.{w}\nThe pressure not to write any of this down, and treat me like a subject, must be relieving.
column6: 我点头，告诉他一个关于我的随意小事。无伤大雅，很小的事。{w}\n他笑了，我们开始交换彼此的信息。他看起来真的很开心。{w}\n不必把这些记下来、不必把我当研究对象，这对他来说一定很轻松。

column5: Everyone always treats me with such apprehension, you know?\nLike — anything they tell me — I'll turn around and use it against them.\nThat {i}is{/i} a part of my business, but it's not like I want to do things that way.
column6: 大家总是对我提心吊胆，你知道吗？\n就像——他们告诉我的任何事——我都会转头拿来对付他们。\n那{i}确实{/i}是我生意的一部分，但我并不想那样做事。

column5: I hope people don't treat me that way after the war is over.\nI'm quitting this swindler's life as soon as I get the chance.\nI'll still write, but I won't use information as a weapon. Ever.
column6: 我希望战争结束后人们不会那样对我。\n一有机会我就退出这种骗子生涯。\n我还是会写东西，但我不会再把情报当武器。绝不。

column5: Instead, I'll use it to help those in need. \nYou know, I've done it before, and it feels good.\nInformation can either be a sharp knife, or a warm embrace.
column6: 相反，我会用它帮助有需要的人。\n你知道，我以前做过，感觉很好。\n情报可以是锋利的刀，也可以是温暖的拥抱。

column5: Weird metaphor, I know, but like I said — I'm no fiction writer.\nI prefer to focus on stuff that's real. Like people, and their actions.\nThey ripple outwards, affecting people in ways they'd never know.
column6: 比喻很怪，我知道，但就像我说的——我不是写小说的。\n我更喜欢关注真实的东西。比如人，还有他们的行为。\n它们向外扩散，以当事人永远不知道的方式影响着别人。

column5: Of course, that's something that applies to \"normal\" people.\nThere's nothing normal about you, [firstname]. No offense, of course.\nYou're going to be in charge of the entire world after this war is over.
column6: 当然，那是适用于“普通”人的道理。\n你一点都不普通，[firstname]。当然，无意冒犯。\n这场战争结束后，你要掌管整个世界。

column5: Wow, talk about putting the pressure on.{w}\nPro senses this, and changes the subject.
column6: 哇，这可真是给我压力。{w}\n普洛察觉到这点，换了个话题。

column5: Can I tell you a little secret?\nMaybe it'll make you see things differently.\nYou know — so you won't picture me as a bad person.
column6: 我能告诉你一个小秘密吗？\n也许会让你换个角度看事情。\n你知道——这样你就不会把我想成坏人。

column5: I can tell that a lot of people do, even if they don't say it.\nBut all I'm doing is helping Damek win this war in the best way I can.\nIt's not my fault that I'm like this. All I can do is play with the hand I've been dealt.
column6: 我看得出很多人就是这么想的，哪怕他们不说。\n但我所做的只是用我能做到的最好方式帮达梅克赢得这场战争。\n我变成这样不是我的错。我能做的只是打好手里这副牌。

column5: He smiles, but suddenly a wave of fear overtakes my entire body.{w}\nI shut my eyes tightly as that last phrase echoes through my mind.\nWhere did I hear that before...? Oh, right — during my visions.
column6: 他笑了笑，但突然一阵恐惧袭遍我全身。{w}\n我紧紧闭上眼，最后一句话在脑海中回响。\n我在哪儿听过这句话……？哦，对了——在我的幻象里。

column5: When I first touched The Blade of Exodus, back in Valinorth.{w}\nThe series of visions ended with me getting stabbed by a man.{w}\nA man, that unfortunately, I'm now able to identify as Pro...
column6: 在我第一次触碰“流亡之刃”时，就在瓦利诺斯。{w}\n那一系列幻象以我被一个男人刺中而结束。{w}\n很不幸，现在我能认出那个男人是普洛……

column5: He lets out a loud sigh, and slowly rests his hand on top of mine.{w}\nA few moments later, he intertwines his fingers with mine, smiling.{w}\nMy heart beats incredibly fast, as this revelation processes itself.
column6: 他重重叹了口气，慢慢把手覆在我的手上。{w}\n过了一会儿，他微笑着与我十指相扣。{w}\n随着这个发现慢慢消化，我的心跳得飞快。

column5: He lets out a soft laugh, and rests his hands behind his head, laying back.{w}\nMy heart beats incredibly fast, as this revelation slowly processes itself in my head.{w}\nThe final vision The Monarchy had given me, was of Pro betraying all of us...?
column6: 他轻笑一声，双手枕在脑后，向后躺下。{w}\n随着这个发现在我脑中慢慢消化，我的心跳得飞快。{w}\n王室给我的最后一段幻象，是普洛背叛我们所有人……？

column5: What was going on...? Why would he do that...?
column6: 这是怎么回事……？他为什么要那样做……？

column5: There was this little boy, who got abandoned by his parents.\nHe didn't know why, and that hurt him so much. Maybe they just didn't want him.\nBut why...? What did he ever do to them? It made no sense, and he hated that.
column6: 从前有个小男孩，被父母抛弃了。\n他不知道为什么，那让他非常痛苦。也许他们就是不想要他。\n可是为什么……？他对他们做过什么？这毫无道理，而他恨透了这一点。

column5: He had to grow up on the streets, living on the scraps that other people threw away.\nIt wasn't just his parents, you know. It almost seemed like nobody wanted him at all.\nThat just made things worse. Can you imagine feeling unwanted by the world...?
column6: 他不得不在街头长大，靠别人扔掉的食物残渣过活。\n不只是他的父母，你知道。几乎好像根本没人想要他。\n这让事情更糟。你能想象被整个世界嫌弃的感觉吗……？

column5: As he starts telling me this story, the anxiety slowly dissipates.{w}\nPro was a swindler, right? Maybe he was only pretending to kill me.{w}\nI don't think Pro could hurt me. There must be a deeper meaning here.
column6: 当他开始讲这个故事时，我的焦虑慢慢消散。{w}\n普洛是个骗子，对吧？也许他只是假装要杀我。{w}\n我不觉得普洛会伤害我。这里一定有更深的含义。

column5: He started to pick up on people's secrets. You know, just little things.\nAfter a while, he found out that people would pay anything to learn these secrets.\nAs a teenager, he used this ability to live a luxurious life of gluttony and sloth.
column6: 他开始打探人们的秘密。你知道，都是些小事。\n过了一阵，他发现人们愿意付出任何代价来得知这些秘密。\n少年时，他靠这项本事过着暴食与懒惰的奢华生活。

column5: He knew secrets that could topple cities, or destroy people's relationships.\nBut none of that gave him satisfaction, because there was {i}one{/i} thing he never knew.\nWhy his parents abandoned him. Why they didn't want him. Did he deserve it...?
column6: 他知道能颠覆城市、摧毁人际关系的秘密。\n但这些都没给他满足感，因为有{i}一件{/i}事他永远不知道。\n他的父母为什么抛弃他。他们为什么不想要他。是他活该吗……？

column5: It was too humiliating to admit, so he made up another story.\nHis parents died during The Occupation. That was much less embarrassing.\nEverybody believed him, and that helped him fit in with a {i}new{/i} group of people.
column6: 承认这个太丢人，所以他编了另一个故事。\n他的父母在“占领”期间死了。这远没那么难堪。\n所有人都相信了他，这也帮他融入了{i}一群新人{/i}。

column5: This new group of people, The Rebellion, wanted to use his skills for good.\nThey accepted him with open arms, which is something nobody had ever done before.\nHe knew he found his place in the world, and since then, he's served this new family.
column6: 这群新人——反抗军——想用他的本事来做善事。\n他们张开双臂接纳了他，这是以前从没有人做过的事。\n他知道自己找到了在世上的一席之地，从那以后，他一直侍奉这个新家庭。

column5: He keeps prodding the locals for information, picking up all sorts of secrets.\nHe wants to know why people do the things they do — and what motivates them.\nHe does this so nobody has to suffer like he did. Simply {i}not{/i} knowing the reason.
column6: 他不断向当地人打探消息，搜集各种各样的秘密。\n他想知道人们为什么做那些事——是什么驱动着他们。\n他这样做，是为了没人再像他那样痛苦。仅仅因为{i}不知道{/i}原因。

column5: I notice he starts to get sad, and tears are forming in his eyes.{w}\nHe's talking about himself. He's the boy in the story, I can tell.{w}\nPerhaps telling me as if it were a story made it easier for him.
column6: 我注意到他开始难过，眼里泛起泪水。{w}\n他是在说他自己。我看得出，他就是故事里的那个男孩。{w}\n也许把它当作故事来讲，对他来说更容易些。

column5: So everybody thinks this guy is bad. A blackmailer, and a swindler.\nThey might be right, but it's just how he grew up. He had no control.\nHe had nobody to show him how to act. Nobody to care, or love him.
column6: 所以所有人都觉得这家伙是坏人。一个敲诈犯，一个骗子。\n他们也许说得对，但他就是这么长大的。他无从选择。\n没人教他该怎么做人。没人在乎他，也没人爱他。

column5: At least, until now...
column6: 至少，直到现在……

column5: He squeezes my hand tighter, and then sits up on the bed.{w}\nResting on his knees, he makes sure his face is level to mine.
column6: 他更紧地握住我的手，然后在床上坐起来。{w}\n他跪坐着，让自己的脸与我的齐平。

column5: I'm sure you've already guessed it, but the boy is me.\nEvery action has a reason. Even mine, as bad as the actions are.\nI only want to see my parents again, face to face — and ask them.
column6: 我确定你已经猜到了，那个男孩就是我。\n每个行为都有原因。即使是像我这样恶劣的行为。\n我只想再见父母一面，面对面——然后问他们。

column5: Why did they hate me...?\nWhy did they throw me away like garbage?\nIf they weren't proud of me, are they proud now...?
column6: 他们为什么恨我……？\n他们为什么像扔垃圾一样把我扔掉？\n如果他们不曾以我为傲，那现在呢……？

column5: I'd do anything to learn where they are right now.\nFollow any order, take any course of action.\nI hope you can understand, [firstname].
column6: 为了知道他们现在在哪，我什么都愿意做。\n服从任何命令，采取任何行动。\n希望你能理解，[firstname]。

column5: I nod, and raise my free hand up to stroke the side of his face.{w}\nHe lets out a soft gasp in response, and looks directly in my eyes.
column6: 我点头，抬起空着的手轻抚他的脸颊。{w}\n他轻吸一口气作为回应，直直看进我的眼睛。

column5: Thank you...
column6: 谢谢你……

column5: I lean in closer, lowering my hand down to his side.{w}\nWe kiss, and I can feel him tremble softly, as if he's shy.{w}\nA single tear trails from his eyes as our lips press together.
column6: 我凑得更近，把手放低到他身侧。{w}\n我们接吻，我能感觉到他轻轻颤抖，仿佛很害羞。{w}\n双唇相触时，一滴泪从他眼角滑落。

column5: No matter what happened — he'd always be welcome at my side.{w}\nWe continue to kiss, the sweet scent of the candle slowly filling the room.{w}\nThe perfect atmosphere, the perfect mood, to express our feelings for one another.
column6: 无论发生什么——他永远都欢迎留在我身边。{w}\n我们继续亲吻，蜡烛的甜香慢慢充满房间。{w}\n完美的氛围，完美的情绪，去表达我们对彼此的感情。

column5: Until The Rebellion took him in, of course.\nI'm sure you already guessed it, but that boy is me.\nAll of my actions, however bad, have had a reason.
column6: 当然，直到反抗军收留了他。\n我确定你已经猜到了，那个男孩就是我。\n我所有的行为，无论多坏，都有原因。

column5: I want to keep going, until I learn about my parents.\nWhere are they now...? Why did they throw me away...?\nIf they weren't proud of me, then would they be proud now?
column6: 我想继续走下去，直到查明我父母的事。\n他们现在在哪……？他们为什么把我扔掉……？\n如果他们不曾以我为傲，那现在会吗？

column5: I hope you can understand. I really do.\nI'd do anything to learn where they are right now. I'd follow any order.\nI just want to see them face to face, and finally learn the reason why.
column6: 希望你能理解。真的。\n为了知道他们现在在哪，我什么都愿意做。我会服从任何命令。\n我只想面对面见到他们，最终弄清原因。

column5: That's why I threw myself into this world of secrets, and trickery.\nI thought that if I kept going, maybe one day, I'd learn the truth.\nI guess we'll find out before this war is over. Right, [firstname]...?
column6: 这就是为什么我投身于这个充满秘密和诡计的世界。\n我想，如果我继续下去，也许有一天能得知真相。\n我猜我们会在战争结束前弄明白。对吧，[firstname]……？

column5: I nod, and give him a soft smile. It meant a lot that he opened up to me.{w}\nIt must suck to not know the truth of something like that. I can't even imagine.{w}\nBut it explains why he's so obsessed with learning about actions and motivations.
column6: 我点头，给他一个温柔的微笑。他向我敞开心扉，这对我意义重大。{w}\n这种事不知道真相一定很难受。我甚至无法想象。{w}\n但这也解释了他为什么如此执着于探究行为和动机。

column5: We talk for a bit longer, about nothing important, before parting ways.{w}\nPerhaps he wanted to ease the tension in the room after dropping those facts.{w}\nAfter we're done, he seems happy, and we seem closer. There was no loss here, today.
column6: 我们又聊了一会儿，没什么重要的，然后各自离开。{w}\n也许他抛下那些事实后，想缓解房里的紧张气氛。{w}\n聊完后，他看起来很开心，我们也似乎更亲近了。今天在这里，没有损失。

column5: We enter the outskirts of Valinorth, and take in deep breaths.{w}\nThe air is so fresh, and pure. It's almost hard to explain.{w}\nHowever, our enjoyment is hindered by Zamira's worried look.
column6: 我们走进瓦利诺斯的外围，深吸一口气。{w}\n空气如此清新纯净。几乎难以形容。{w}\n然而，扎米拉担忧的神色打断了我们的享受。

column5: Well, what's the news?\nIs everything okay, Zamira?
column6: 那么，有什么消息？\n一切还好吗，扎米拉？

column5: I guess everything is fine — technically.\nIt's just something I need to tell you in private.\nThe villagers will have enough on their plates tonight.
column6: 我想一切都还好——严格来说。\n只是有件事我得私下跟你们说。\n村民们今晚已经够多事要操心了。

column5: So it's something that affects them, too?
column6: 所以这也是会影响到他们的事？

column5: More than that, actually.\nLook, I'll be completely honest with you.\nI'm sure Valinorth will be resettled in the future.
column6: 其实不止如此。\n听着，我会对你们完全坦诚。\n我相信瓦利诺斯将来会重新安置。

column5: I'm glad you think so, Zamira.\nI was starting to worry about everything.\nIt seems like Mylus has everything under control.
column6: 很高兴你这么想，扎米拉。\n我本来开始担心一切了。\n看来迈勒斯把一切都掌控得很好。

column5: Yeah, about that...\nThis is where it gets a little awkward.\nYou see, he didn't really tell you everything.
column6: 是啊，关于这个……\n这就有点尴尬了。\n你看，他其实没把一切都告诉你们。

column5: What...? Really?
column6: 什么……？真的？

column5: This is starting to get pretty overwhelming!\nHe seemed pretty open. What was he hiding?\nI don't think I can handle another \"revelation\".
column6: 这开始让人有点招架不住了！\n他看起来挺坦率的。他隐瞒了什么？\n我觉得我承受不了又一个“真相大揭秘”了。

column5: It was probably too embarrassing for him to admit.\nBut he doesn't really want to lead Valinorth anymore.\nHe told me when he gets to Mazeo, he's staying for good.
column6: 大概是太难堪了，他不好意思承认。\n但他其实不想再领导瓦利诺斯了。\n他告诉我，到了马泽奥他就要永久留下。

column5: That can't be true...
column6: 不可能吧……

column5: He was doing such a good job!
column6: 他做得那么好！

column5: He was, but I understand where he's coming from.\nIt's possible to be good at something you don't enjoy.\nHe deserves a fresh start. A pursuit of his own choosing.
column6: 是，但我理解他的想法。\n擅长一件事，不等于你必须喜欢它。\n他该有一个新的开始。追求他自己选择的东西。

column5: I guess so. Then what about resettling Valinorth?\nWho'd be in charge when that happens?
column6: 我想也是。那瓦利诺斯重新安置怎么办？\n到时候谁来负责？

column5: People would migrate back too slowly.\nWe'd be in no shape to hold a formal election.\nSo correct me if I'm wrong, but that means...
column6: 人们迁回来会很慢。\n我们也没条件举行正式选举。\n所以如果我没说错，那意味着……

column5: Bingo!
column6: 答对了！

column5: [firstname]...
column6: [firstname]……

column5: [firstname]...
column6: [firstname]……

column5: Does somebody want to fill me in?
column6: 有人愿意跟我解释一下吗？

column5: Matters of Valinorth's future...\nWith no Elder, they're under the jurisdiction of [firstname].\nBelieve it or not, {i}he{/i} gets to choose the next leader.
column6: 瓦利诺斯的未来事务……\n没有长老，就归[firstname]管辖。\n信不信由你，{i}他{/i}能选定下一位领袖。

column5: Matters of Valinorth's future...\nWith no Elder, they're under the jurisdiction of [firstname].\nBelieve it or not, {i}she{/i} gets to choose the next Elder.
column6: 瓦利诺斯的未来事务……\n没有长老，就归[firstname]管辖。\n信不信由你，{i}她{/i}能选定下一任长老。

column5: A contingency plan for special cases like this.\nThe only condition is that you can't choose {i}yourself{/i}.\nYour duty and role in Valinorth is already well established.
column6: 这是为这类特殊情况准备的应急方案。\n唯一的条件是你不能选{i}你自己{/i}。\n你在瓦利诺斯的职责和角色早已明确。

column5: Take your time, evaluate the candidates, and think about it.\nAgain, it's not really {i}bad{/i} news, it's just another change.
column6: 慢慢来，评估候选人，好好想想。\n再说一次，这其实不算{i}坏{/i}消息，只是又一次变化。

column5: There's really nothing to think about, though.\nChoose me! Then I won't be the third wheel anymore.\nWe can be a trio — and work together all the time!
column6: 其实根本没什么好想的。\n选我吧！那我就不会再是多余的那个了。\n我们可以成为三人组——一直一起共事！

column5: Hey now, let's not jump to conclusions.\nI think I'd be a fine candidate for Elder.\nFortaime was {i}trained{/i} to fill the gap I'd leave.
column6: 嘿，别急着下结论。\n我觉得我会是长老的合适人选。\n福泰姆是{i}受过训练{/i}来填补我留下的空缺的。

column5: Oh my. I should've expected this.\nSorry to put you in an awkward situation.
column6: 哎呀。我早该料到会这样。\n抱歉让你陷入尴尬的处境。

column5: It's only awkward if Valessa makes it awkward!
column6: 只有瓦莱莎觉得尴尬，它才尴尬！

column5: Hmph. Whatever!
column6: 哼。随便吧！

column5: They cross their arms and turn away from each other.{w}\nFighting over an opening that was only revealed seconds ago?{w}\nI could understand their passion, but we needed unity right now.
column6: 他们抱起手臂，背过身去。{w}\n为一个几秒前才刚揭晓的空缺争吵？{w}\n我能理解他们的热情，但我们现在需要团结。

column5: Look, this might not be relevant for years to come.\nThere's no need to argue about this. Stay focused.\nWe have a really important job on our hands, you know.
column6: 听着，这事可能几年内都不会有影响。\n没必要为这个争。保持专注。\n我们手上可是有一件非常重要的事。

column5: They don't respond, and simply retain their pose.{w}\nTheir passion for Valinorth is admirable, but intrusive.{w}\nWe had a clear goal, and now things were getting muddied.
column6: 他们没有回应，只是保持着那副姿势。{w}\n他们对瓦利诺斯的热情令人钦佩，却也碍事。{w}\n我们本有明确的目标，现在事情却变得混乱了。

column5: None of you know where Peregrino is, right?\nIf I start walking without you, you'll get lost.\nI'll give you a few minutes, but I'm on a schedule.
column6: 你们都不知道佩雷格里诺在哪，对吧？\n要是我自己先走，你们会迷路的。\n我给你们几分钟，但我有日程安排。

column5: The threat makes them both turn back around.
column6: 这句威胁让他们俩都转回了身。

column5: Good. That's what I thought.\nTake a few moments to talk amongst yourselves.\nBut when you're ready to go, we need to move as fast as we can.
column6: 很好。我就知道。\n花几分钟你们自己聊聊。\n但准备好出发时，我们得尽快行动。

column5: Alright.
column6: 好吧。

column5: Yeah, fair enough.
column6: 嗯，有道理。

column5: Zamira rests against a nearby tree, and lets out a loud sigh.{w}\nHe was just relaying information. The fallout wasn't his to deal with.{w}\nWe have a few minutes to spare. I should make the most of it.
column6: 扎米拉靠在旁边一棵树上，重重叹了口气。{w}\n他只是传个话而已。后果不该由他承担。{w}\n我们还有几分钟空闲。我该好好利用。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Yeah, of course I do!\nIf I become Elder, then Fortaime can take over as your Scribe.\nIt seems like the logical course of action, doesn't it?
column6: 当然，我当然愿意！\n如果我当上长老，福泰姆就可以接任你的书记官。\n这似乎是最合乎逻辑的做法，不是吗？

column5: We need to figure out how to save Valinorth.\nAfter the attack, we can rebuild from the ashes.\nBut I also want to solve our problem with the spirits.
column6: 我们得想办法拯救瓦利诺斯。\n袭击之后，我们可以从灰烬中重建。\n但我也想解决我们与灵之间的问题。

column5: Once we restore our connection, we'll be fine.\nAfter that, it's just a matter of what we do with our nation.\nI'm not really a fan of what Mylus and his Father did.
column6: 一旦我们恢复了联系，就没事了。\n之后，就只是我们该怎么对待自己的国家了。\n我不太认同迈勒斯和他父亲的做法。

column5: Well, they sacrificed Valinorth's independence.\nThat was the one thing that set us apart — made us unique.\nIf we lose that, we lose Valinorth's very soul.
column6: 嗯，他们牺牲了瓦利诺斯的独立。\n那正是让我们与众不同的东西——让我们独一无二。\n如果我们失去它，就失去了瓦利诺斯的灵魂。

column5: I want to keep our line of Seers going. We can't lose our heritage.\nI'd ensure that we remained non-partisan, just like always.\nLook at all the trouble these \"alliances\" have given us.
column6: 我想让我们的先知血脉延续下去。我们不能丢掉传承。\n我会确保我们一如既往地保持不结盟。\n看看这些“联盟”给我们惹了多少麻烦。

column5: I'm glad you feel the same way.\nWe were fine on our own, for generations.\nIt was Mylus and his Father that got us caught up in politics.
column6: 很高兴你也这么想。\n我们独自屹立了几代人，都好好的。\n是迈勒斯和他父亲把我们卷进了政治。

column5: Without that, we'd be safe and sound.\nIn fact, we'd be celebrating your induction right now!\nI see independence and strength under {i}my{/i} leadership.
column6: 没有那些，我们本可以安然无恙。\n事实上，我们现在本可以在庆祝你的就任仪式！\n在{i}我{/i}的领导下，我看到的是独立与强大。

column5: Strength doesn't come from numbers, though.\nIt comes with the ability to be ourselves. To express what's inside.\nWithout our independence, we're no different from anyone else.
column6: 不过，力量并非来自人数。\n它来自做自己的能力。表达内心的能力。\n没有独立，我们和任何人都没有区别。

column5: Our line of Seers would lose meaning. Our forests would be cut down.\nAfter a few decades, we'd be no different than Mazeo.\nWe can't lose this beauty. I'll fight to keep it safe.
column6: 我们的先知血脉会失去意义。我们的森林会被砍伐。\n几十年后，我们就会和马泽奥没什么两样。\n我们不能失去这份美丽。我会为守护它而战。

column5: There's really no right or wrong answer.\nIt's just a matter of preference. It could go either way.\nAs long as the leader is capable, Valinorth will be fine.
column6: 其实没有对错之分。\n只是偏好问题。两种都可以。\n只要领袖有能力，瓦利诺斯就会没事。

column5: But you should choose either me or Fortaime.\nWe're both trained, and intimately familiar with Valinorth.\nWe studied with Mylus all the time. We can do this, trust me.
column6: 但你该选我或福泰姆。\n我们都受过训练，对瓦利诺斯了如指掌。\n我们一直跟迈勒斯学习。我们能胜任，相信我。

column5: I don't know. But if it's possible, I'll do it.\nI'll look for reading material when we get to Mazeo.\nOr if we ever find ourselves in Balteus, there's the Grand Library.
column6: 我不知道。但如果有可能，我会去做。\n到了马泽奥我会去找阅读材料。\n要是我们哪天真到了巴尔泰乌斯，那里有大图书馆。

column5: Remember, that power still exists within you.\nAfter we defeat The Triumvirate, it won't just vanish.\nThere must be a way to put it back in the Spirit Idol.
column6: 记住，那股力量仍然存在于你体内。\n打败三人执政团之后，它不会就此消失。\n一定有办法把它放回灵像里。

column5: We definitely will. We can't just let Valinorth die.\nEven if it takes the rest of my life, I'll keep searching.\nI just hope that you'll stay with me along the way.
column6: 我们一定会的。我们不能就这么让瓦利诺斯死去。\n哪怕要花掉我余生，我也会继续寻找。\n我只希望这一路上你能陪着我。

column5: Nothing is impossible, you know.\nThat's just something people say when they don't want to try.\nIf we put all of our effort into it? We can save Valinorth.
column6: 没有什么是不可能的，你知道。\n那只是人们不想尝试时说的话。\n如果我们全力以赴？我们能拯救瓦利诺斯。

column5: What!? Why would you say something like that...?\nIt's not like you to give up so easily.\nWe'll come back from this, stronger than ever.
column6: 什么！？你怎么会说这种话……？\n这么轻易放弃可不像你。\n我们会从这件事中恢复过来，比以前更强大。

column5: In fact, I'm so certain, I'm changing the subject.\nI refuse to talk about such negative things.
column6: 事实上，我这么确定，所以要换个话题。\n我拒绝谈这么消极的事情。

column5: Maybe a couple of hours, if we walk fast.\nIt's a longer trek from there to Mazeo, though.\nI've never been — but I've seen maps and read books.
column6: 如果我们走得快，也许几个小时。\n不过从那里到马泽奥路途更远。\n我从没去过——但我看过地图，读过书。

column5: It's not exactly my kind of place.\nI've never had the urge to drink ale, or wine.\nLet alone the urge to walk such a long distance.
column6: 那不太算是我喜欢的地方。\n我从没想过要喝麦酒或葡萄酒。\n更别说想走那么远的路了。

column5: It's not that I won't. I just don't feel compelled to.\nMaybe I'll feel different when we actually get there.\nI feel like we have more pressing matters at hand.
column6: 不是我不愿意。我只是没有那种冲动。\n也许真到了那里我会有不同的感觉。\n我觉得我们手头有更紧迫的事。

column5: It's probably for the best.\nThere's too much we need to take care of.\nMaybe we'll feel different when this is all over.
column6: 大概这样最好。\n我们要操心的事太多了。\n也许等这一切结束后我们的感觉会不同。

column5: Hmm? What about it?
column6: 嗯？怎么了？

column5: They usually are.\nIt's not like an argument between us is anything new.\nWith a few minutes to cool off, everything will be fine.
column6: 通常都是这样。\n我们之间的争吵又不是什么新鲜事。\n冷静几分钟，一切就没事了。

column5: Besides, we all know what the right choice is.\nI'm the most qualified person in Valinorth to replace Mylus.\nFortaime is trained to replace me. It just seems natural.
column6: 再说，我们都知道正确的选择是什么。\n我是瓦利诺斯最有资格接替迈勒斯的人。\n福泰姆受训是为了接替我。这看起来顺理成章。

column5: Oh, of course I am!\nI work with Mylus almost every day. I know exactly what he does.\nIn a way, he trained me, just like his Father trained {i}him{/i}.
column6: 哦，我当然能胜任！\n我几乎每天都和迈勒斯一起工作。我清楚他做的一切。\n某种程度上，是他训练了我，就像他父亲训练{i}他{/i}一样。

column5: If you chose Fortaime, there'd be a learning curve.\nThat, and I don't think he's fully qualified.\nMake sure not to tell him that. He'll freak out.
column6: 如果你选福泰姆，会有个学习过程。\n而且，我觉得他并不完全够格。\n千万别告诉他这话。他会炸毛的。

column5: His contact with Mylus was minimal compared to mine.\nIf he took over, he'd need to be trained from the ground up.\nBut if Mylus is retiring, I don't think he'd be willing to teach.
column6: 他跟迈勒斯的接触比我少得多。\n如果由他接手，得从头开始培训。\n但如果迈勒斯要退休了，我不觉得他愿意教。

column5: And with no teacher, you need to find somebody already trained.\nI have a pretty good idea of what Mylus does. I saw him every day.\nSo I'm trained, and ready to lead. Seems like an easy choice, right?
column6: 没有老师，你就得找一个已经受过训练的人。\n我很清楚迈勒斯做的事。我每天都见他。\n所以我受过训练，准备好领导了。看起来选择很简单，对吧？

column5: I'm not sure about that, actually!\nIt would be counterproductive though.\nYou already have two perfect candidates!
column6: 其实我不太确定！\n不过那样会适得其反。\n你已经有两位完美的人选了！

column5: We're high up on Valinorth's ladder. Not many people are.\nI also think that the villagers would support both of us.\nIt seems like a natural succession of power to me.
column6: 我们在瓦利诺斯的层级里位置很高。没多少人能这样。\n我也觉得村民们会支持我们俩。\n在我看来，这就是自然而然的权力传承。

column5: I've been thinking about that, actually.\nNot just you, but Damek as well...?\nOnly a Seer of Valinorth can have visions.
column6: 其实我也一直在想这个问题。\n不只是你，还有达梅克……？\n只有瓦利诺斯的先知才能拥有幻象。

column5: Is there more to Damek than we know...?\nOr is there more to the blade than we know?\nI'd say it's the energy inside of you, but Damek doesn't have that.
column6: 达梅克身上有我们不知道的东西吗……？\n还是那把剑有我们不知道的东西？\n我会说是你体内的能量，但达梅克没有那个。

column5: Or does he...?\nBasically, none of this makes any sense to me.\nWe're watching the laws of Alestia be remade before us.
column6: 还是说他有……？\n基本上，这对我来说毫无道理。\n我们正看着阿莱斯蒂亚的法则在眼前被重写。

column5: So if you're asking me for an answer, I really don't know.\nIt's something we'll have to learn as we venture forward.\nBut I have a feeling that this blade changes {i}everything{/i}.
column6: 所以如果你是在问我答案，我真的不知道。\n这是我们前进途中要去弄明白的事。\n但我有种感觉，这把剑会改变{i}一切{/i}。

column5: Hey.
column6: 嘿。

column5: Wait, is this like a job interview or something?\nI've never been very good at \"selling\" myself.\nFirst and foremost though, I'd reconnect with the spirits.
column6: 等等，这算是面试之类的吗？\n我一直不太擅长“推销”自己。\n不过首先，我会重新连接灵。

column5: That way, Valinorth wouldn't freeze over.\nA lot of people forget it's the spirits that keep us warm.\nAfter that, I guess I'd focus on what to do with the people.
column6: 这样，瓦利诺斯就不会冻住了。\n很多人忘了是灵让我们保持温暖。\n之后，我想我会专注于如何安置人民。

column5: Actually, I'm not too sure about that.\nBut we're about to go on a huge journey.\nI'll make sure to pay attention along the way.
column6: 其实，这个我不太确定。\n但我们即将踏上一次巨大的旅程。\n我会一路留心。

column5: If the connection can be taken away, it can be given back.\nThere's nothing that says this is a one way street.\nSo take care of that power until we can put it back!
column6: 如果这份联系能被夺走，就也能被归还。\n没谁说这是条单行道。\n所以在我们能还回去之前，好好保管那股力量！

column5: That's the spirit!\nSaving Alestia comes first, but Valinorth is still important.\nThere has to be a way to do both at the same time, you know?
column6: 这才对！\n拯救阿莱斯蒂亚优先，但瓦利诺斯依然重要。\n总得有办法两件事同时兼顾，你知道吗？

column5: What!? No way!\nYou might feel that way, but I don't.\nIf I were the Elder, I'd do anything to save Valinorth!
column6: 什么！？不可能！\n你也许那么想，但我不。\n如果我是长老，我会不惜一切拯救瓦利诺斯！

column5: Well, we have an important choice to make.\nWe can follow after Mylus, and drop our independence.\nOr we can distance ourselves from the other nations, like always.
column6: 嗯，我们有个重要的选择要做。\n我们可以追随迈勒斯，放弃独立。\n或者像往常一样，与其他国家保持距离。

column5: Right now, I think unity is important.\nIf I were The Elder, I'd band our world together.\nWe could live in harmony, and trade freely!
column6: 现在，我觉得团结很重要。\n如果我是长老，我会把我们的世界凝聚在一起。\n我们可以和谐共处，自由通商！

column5: I know I hate the trade ban they put on Mazeo, but this isn't personal.\nLifting those bans and uniting the nations would create peace.\nIsn't that our goal at the end of this, [firstname]?
column6: 我知道我讨厌他们对马泽奥实施的贸易禁令，但这不是私人恩怨。\n解除那些禁令、团结各国，会带来和平。\n这不就是我们最终的目标吗，[firstname]？
